title: Diamondbacks-Nationals updates. Source says Sox deal not option
description: The Diamondbacks will be looking to secure another series victory when they play the rubber match against the Nationals on Sunday, July 26.
fullText:
WASHINGTON — The late-night trade on Saturday, July 25, pulled off by the Washington Nationals, in which they acquired a young starting pitcher, Connelly Early, from the Boston Red Sox, was just the sort of deal the Diamondbacks have interest in doing ahead of next week’s trade deadline.

The Diamondbacks spoke to the Red Sox about that kind of trade, according to a source, but were told Boston was not interested in acquiring a player who skewed more toward prospect status. In exchange for Early, the Red Sox acquired infielder Curtis Mead, who has had a breakout season in the majors for the Nationals, hitting .254/.352/.500 with 17 homers.

It is unclear who among their young hitters the Diamondbacks would have considered moving, but prospects/young major leaguers such as Ryan Waldschmidt, Tommy Troy, Tim Tawa, etc., apparently were not established enough in the Red Sox’s eyes, the source said.

The Diamondbacks spoke with the Red Sox during the offseason about a possible Ketel Marte trade but were not able to come to an agreement.

Diamondbacks right-hander Michael Soroka threw a two-inning, 35-pitch live batting practice session on Saturday, July 25, the club said.

Soroka is lined up to throw a bullpen session on Monday, July 27, and is expected to pitch in a bridge league game — a game at a spring training complex likely to feature mostly young minor leaguers — in his next outing.

Right-hander Justin Martinez threw a bullpen session on Saturday and will pitch in a bridge league game on Tuesday, July 28.

Outfielder Jordan Lawlar took five at-bats at the complex as he works his way back from a hamstring injury.

The Diamondbacks gave the green light to Double-A center fielder Druw Jones to be away from his Amarillo team for the weekend to attend the Hall of Fame induction of his father, Andruw Jones, in Cooperstown, N.Y.

“He reached out to me earlier in the month and just asked if he could go for it,” Diamondbacks farm director Chris Slivka said. “That’s obviously a once-in-a-lifetime experience to go support your dad.”

Jones, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 draft, has had an up-and-down season with Amarillo. His overall stat line is pedestrian at best for a good hitting environment — .259/.372/.353 with five homers and 23 steals — but Slivka said there has been significant growth under the hood.

“There's been a lot of positives,” Slivka said. “Cleaning up the lower half (swing) mechanics a little bit, he’s starting to use the ground a little more, riding out his back side, more adjustable front to back.

“The last couple of months has been really promising. He was getting into a pretty good rhythm, too, before he (left for Cooperstown). You’re starting to see more power emerge, starting to see him hit for a little more power to the pull side. … It’s all trending in the right direction, and the swing looks better. He has put in a lot of hard work. Credit to him.”

Diamondbacks LHP Kohl Drake (0-0, 1.80) vs. Nationals RHP Miles Mikolas (3-7, 5.60).

At Nationals Park: Drake was effective in his major league debut last week at Chase Field, where he held the Athletics to one run over five innings, walking two, hitting one batter and striking out five. … He elicited a surprising amount of whiffs, getting four swings and misses apiece on his fastball, changeup and cutter and another on his curveball. … Drake had a 6.92 ERA in Triple-A Reno at the time of his call-up, but he had been better (4.70 ERA) over his previous six starts. … Mikolas has been alternating between starting and pitching bulk innings in relief. His results coming out of the bullpen (3.75 ERA) have been far better than as a starter (8.53). … He faced the Diamondbacks twice last year, posting a 5.40 ERA in 10 innings. … 3B Nolan Arenado has gone 6 for 12 with three homers off him.

Monday, July 27: At Pittsburgh, 3:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Merrill Kelly (8-8, 5.12) vs. Pirates RHP Bubba Chandler (3-8, 4.47).

Tuesday, July 28: At Pittsburgh, 3:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Brandon Pfaadt (5-1, 4.43) vs. Pirates RHP Mitch Keller (6-7, 4.90)

Wednesday, July 29: At Pittsburgh, 9:35 a.m., Diamondbacks LHP Eduardo Rodriguez (9-3, 2.64) vs. Pirates RHP Jared Jones (2-1, 3.72).

title: Dark-horse WR may be emerging for Panthers early in training camp
description: We may have an early dark horse on our hands at Panthers training camp.
fullText:
Barring any more major injuries, the Carolina Panthers probably won't have many open spots in their wideout room by the end of the summer. Even still, an unlikely candidate to crack the initial 53-man roster may be making his case for one of those jobs.

Sunday's outing of training camp was won by a bounce-back performance from the Carolina offense. Among the stars on the morning was second-year receiver Ja'seem Reed, who head coach Dave Canales talked about during his post-practice press conference.

"He's consistent," Canales stated. "He knows the concepts, he's a really smart guy—and he's been that way since we got him. A guy we have a lot of trust in. And then, he just keeps making plays."

The 6-foot-2, 195-pound Reed was making plays at the University of San Diego in 2024, the year before entering the pros. He reeled in 77 receptions for 1,052 yards and 12 touchdowns—earning the Pioneer Football League Offensive Player of the Year honors in the process.

Reed would then initially be signed by the Cleveland Browns as an undrafted free agent in 2025. After he was waived off injured reserve in June, the Panthers brought Reed in at the end of July—and kept him on their practice squad through his rookie campaign.

As the landscape stands, there may be only one or two Week 1 jerseys up for grabs at wide receiver—with Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Chris Brazzell II, David Moore as probable locks. In addition to Reed, the Panthers will also have to figure out the placements for the likes of special teams stud Brycen Tremayne, 2025 sixth-round pick Jimmy Horn Jr. and free-agent addition John Metchie III.

While Reed does have his work cut out for him, he's off to an intriguing start—and could be more than just a practice-squad player come September.

title: Celtic Keep Close Tabs On The Lazio Pair: Why They Must Snap Up At Least One Of The Attackers
description: If a recent transfer update from Lorenzo Canicchio on X is true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on the Lazio duo Gustav Isaksen and Matteo Cancellieri. Isaksen, currently injured, is expected to retur...
fullText:
If a recent transfer update from Lorenzo Canicchio on X is true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on the Lazio duo Gustav Isaksen and Matteo Cancellieri. Isaksen, currently injured, is expected to return to action in September, and interest in Cancellieri could heat up soon, with a valuation of around €15m potentially negotiable.

Having progressed through Roslev IK and Midtjylland’s academy ranks, Isaksen broke into the latter’s first-team squad in 2019. He went on to score 33 goals and assist 18 times in 139 games across competitions, and a scintillating 2022-23 season earned him a €14.40m transfer to Serie A giants Lazio in the summer of 2023.

The 25-year-old Denmark international has so far netted 14 times and laid on 11 assists in 121 outings for the Eagles. He has often been rotated with Cancellieri down the right-hand flank, but the club are ready to listen to offers for both if the right bids are tabled in due time.

Born in Rome, the 24-year-old Azzurri international left his boyhood side AS Roma at the age of 18 after a prominent spell with the reserves. He initially joined Hellas Verona on loan, before the move was made permanent for a fee of around €4m. After a sporadic stint, Lazio snapped up Cancellieri on a season-long loan with an obligation-to-buy. Although the deal was made permanent, back-to-back loans were sanctioned to fellow top-flight outfits Empoli and Parma after a difficult 2022-23 campaign. His performance gradually improved with more minutes, thus helping him attain a regular role last season under Maurizio Sarri.

ROME, ITALY – MAY 23: Matteo Cancellieri of SS Lazio competes for the ball with Simone Canestrelli of Pisa SC during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Pisa SC at Stadio Olimpico on May 23, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

While he scored 4 times and assisted twice in 30 Serie A appearances, it remains to be seen whether the new boss, Gennaro Gattuso, sticks with him in the attacking third. Nevertheless, neither Cancellieri nor Isaksen is untouchable, and Celtic, in the hunt for a new right-sided attacker, could rope in either of them to bolster their frontline.

The Hoops are having yet another slow window, with Camilo Duran being the only arrival this summer. But they have parted ways with Daizen Maeda, whereas Kelechi Iheanacho has rejected a contract offer in favour of a transfer to the Turkish second-tier side Bursaspor. Yang Hyun-jun had his moments last season, but they failed to replace Nicolas Kuhn’s productivity from the right.

Cancellieri and Isaksen, both left-footed, prefer to operate as inverted wingers. They like to take on defenders with dribbling, pace, and cut-ins, but their lack of finishing, decision-making, and inconsistent delivery from wide areas must improve to make a mark in Scottish football.

title: Just Being Frank: Blackhawks' Nazar In Position To Make Next Step On And Off Ice
description: Armed with 122 games of NHL experience and a seven-year contract extension, Frank Nazar is ready and willing to be a leader in Chicago’s dressing room
fullText:
Frank Nazar is in the middle of talking about what it meant to have the trust of the Chicago Blackhawks’ coaching staff this season when he lets out a knowing chuckle.

The laugh comes as he’s explaining the importance of this particular off-season. “This summer is extremely important and going to be a good summer to fine-tune things and get better all around,” Nazar said. “The goal is then to come in next year and help the younger guys that are there and try to lead by example.”

Pause. Timeout. The younger guys? Younger than whom, exactly? Because Nazar is not a grizzled vet but rather a fresh-faced 22-year-old with all of 122 big-league games to his name. “No, I know! It does sound ridiculous,” he said. “Technically, two years – two years and a three-game span – that’s going to be old on our team.”

In fairness, Nazar’s not exactly wrong. In Chicago’s season-ender, a win over San Jose, he was older than nearly one-third of Blackhawks skaters, a group that included Connor Bedard and Anton Frondell. And there’s an honest possibility the number of players in Chicago’s lineup who are Nazar’s junior could increase at the start of next season, with the likes of Roman Kantserov, Sacha Boisvert and Marek Vanacker among the roster hopefuls.

And maybe in his mind, and the minds of others, Nazar seems a bit further along in his career than he actually is. After all, there aren’t many players with his resume who’ve already inked a seven-year extension, let alone one valued at nearly $46.2 million.

NHL Prospect Pool Overview '26-27: Chicago Blackhawks Give Young Core Immediate Help The Chicago Blackhawks made two bold decisions by spending a lot to acquire and re-sign Bowen Byram. That said, they still have a high-end prospect pool that Tony Ferrari examines in depth.

Indeed, when Nazar, the 13th overall pick in 2022, signed a long-term extension last August, he did so having played in 56 NHL games. That’s one more game than Wild star Kirill Kaprizov had played before he signed a big-money bridge deal in Minnesota. It’s two more than Mattias Samuelsson had played before the Buffalo Sabres bet big on the blueliner. Comparisons aside, it’s few enough games that, were he anyone else, Nazar might be feeling pressure to perform or the weight of expectation.

Ask Nazar, though, and the contract exists neither as a motivator nor a burden. Sure, he wants to prove he’s worth every penny and more. Yes, he understands that such a signing is rare. But none of it bothers him.

Evaluating The Moves Blackhawks GM Kyle Davidson Has Made This NHL Off-Season The Chicago Blackhawks locked up a key puzzle piece Saturday with a massive new contract extension for superstar center Connor Bedard. Blackhawks GM Kyle Davidson has been one of the NHL's most active GMs this summer. So what Hawks moves are winners – and what moves could Chicago come to regret?

“Really, I try not to focus too much on that,” he said. “If I did want to focus a lot on that, I would have played this whole year and waited to sign. The way guys are signing now, I could have signed for more or tried to push for more, you know? But like I said, I like to focus more on the long scheme of things. I want to win.”

Make no mistake, if the Blackhawks are going to capital-’W’ win, Nazar is going to be at the heart of that success. He’s already proven he can be a shift-by-shift contributor, posting 12 goals and 26 points as a rookie and following it with 15 goals and 41 points in 66 games this season as a sophomore. But Nazar also spent the majority of his minutes playing down the middle and anchoring the second line. In a sense, if Bedard has the superstar style, it’s Nazar – not short on flash of his own, mind you – who provides the substance.

Blackhawks Bring Back Franchise Legend Patrick Kane On Two-Year Deal The Chicago Blackhawks have signed 37-year-old Patrick Kane to a two-year, $8 million AAV contract, bringing the franchise's second-leading point scorer back to Chicago.

That’s something Nazar showcased in his 21 games in the AHL before becoming a full-time big-leaguer in 2024-25, as he played in all situations and at all strengths for Chicago’s affiliate in Rockford. And that has continued in the NHL. Nazar ranked fifth among Hawks forwards in average ice time per game at even strength, third in PP average and fifth in shorthanded average. Whereas some players his age talk about using the summer to build speed, strength or their shot, Nazar is more concerned with consistency, reads and further honing his on-ice smarts. “That’s a big thing that will keep guys in the league for a long time,” he said.

Nazar’s aim, too, is to be around a long time – not just in the league but in Chicago.

As he’s set to begin his seven-year deal, he’s already envisioning himself as a Blackhawk well into the future – even for the rest of his career. And while the first couple of those years haven’t quite gone as planned for the franchise, Nazar sees the foundation of something special. “To find a team where, maybe, things aren’t going exactly the way they want and everyone still stays so close, it’s pretty rare,” he said. “That’s the chemistry and what we’re building here in Chicago. That goes to the GMs and everyone picking the right guys – guys who are not just good players but good off the ice. A lot of guys come in and fit in right away, and it’s been a lot of fun to play with all these guys. I’m super excited. I know things will turn around, but when things turn around and are a little brighter, we’re going to have much more fun.”

title: Giants Make Decision on Potential Jung Hoo Lee Trade: Report
description: The San Francisco Giants are expected to be sellers ahead of the upcoming MLB trade deadline on Aug. 3.That said, which players they are willing to move remains the bigger question, and trade interest has centered around outfielder Jung Hoo Lee, who is in his third season with the organization.Are Giants Shopping Jung Hoo Lee?In […] The post Giants Make Decision on Potential Jung Hoo Lee Trade: Report appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The San Francisco Giants are expected to be sellers ahead of the upcoming MLB trade deadline on Aug. 3.

That said, which players they are willing to move remains the bigger question, and trade interest has centered around outfielder Jung Hoo Lee, who is in his third season with the organization.

In his latest trade intel published by USA Today’s Bob Nightengale on Sunday, the Giants have informed teams that Hoo Lee is unavailable in trade talks but are willing to listen on Heliot Ramos.

“The San Francisco Giants are telling teams that right fielder Jung Hoo Lee is staying, but they will move left fielder Heliot Ramos,” Nightengale reported.

Trade deadline updates, per @BNightengale:

• Giants are telling teams that Jung Hoo Lee is unavailable, but they will trade Heliot Ramos
 • Mets are “desperate to dump” Luis Robert
 • Rival teams believe Twins will trade Ryan Jeffers, with Yankees the leading candidate
 • White…

— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) July 26, 2026

Hoo Lee has been one of the purest hitters in the game this season, currently batting .302 across 96 games and 384 plate appearances.

He has recorded 51 runs, 109 hits, six home runs, and 37 RBIs while slugging .435 and maintaining a .771 OPS.

Lee’s defense has also drawn plenty of praise, including Saturday night when Giants manager Tony Vitello called for him to win a Gold Glove.

“He’s been phenomenal in right field,” Vitello said. “Think back on how many of the big catches he made [swung] the game one way or the other.”

At the moment, the Giants don’t have much to play for unless they can quickly turn things around, as they enter their series finale against the Los Angeles Angels with a 44-60 record despite winning two straight games.

They sit fourth in the NL West and are essentially out of the division race, trailing the Los Angeles Dodgers by 22.5 games. In the Wild Card race, San Francisco sits 10.5 games back.

title: Ben Shelton Addresses Montréal Fiasco After Jannik Sinner Snub – ‘How’s the Guy Going To Play Every Tournament?’
description: Ben Shelton will soon be faced with the task of defending his Masters 1000 trophy in Montréal. Much like his title run in Toronto last year, the American will enter the tournament with the sport’s biggest names, including Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz, and Novak Djokovic, absent from the field.
fullText:
Ben Shelton will soon be faced with the task of defending his Masters 1000 trophy in Montréal. Much like his title run in Toronto last year, the American will enter the tournament with the sport’s biggest names, including Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz, and Novak Djokovic, absent from the field.

While the official reason for Sinner and Djokovic’s withdrawals from the tournament is “change of schedule,” Alcaraz is missing due to his ongoing injury recovery.

The ATP Tour calendar currently includes nine Masters 1000 tournaments. The season begins with the Sunshine Double in Indian Wells and Miami, with both tournaments featuring 96-player draws for more than 20 years. Meanwhile, in an attempt to give lower-ranked players more opportunities, the Madrid Open, Italian Open, and Shanghai Masters — all of which were previously one-week events — joined the club in 2023.

The Cincinnati Open and Canadian Open followed suit last year, expanding into 11-day events. The decision, however, was soon met with criticism from players and fans alike, given the already congested tennis calendar.

When asked about the rising withdrawals ahead of the Mubadala DC Open, Shelton said, “For the tournaments and the players, I’m not sure how sustainable the current setup of the tour is. I think for me the biggest thing I’m seeing is the injuries.”

Long before the draw was expanded to 96 players, the Canadian Open was already facing challenges due to its placement so close to Wimbledon. Sinner, the two-time reigning Wimbledon champion, chose to skip the event to focus on recovery, while Djokovic has not featured at the tournament since 2018.

Ben Shelton pointed out Sinner’s remarkable 44-3 record for 2026 to highlight the number of matches he has played this season. “But then you have a guy like Sinner, who is winning as many matches as he is; his match count is so high. How is the guy going to go and play every tournament? I don’t think it’s sustainable.”

Sinner attempted a non-stop schedule between Indian Wells and the French Open this year, playing six consecutive tournaments. While he won the first five tournaments, the strategy ultimately appeared to backfire as he crashed out in the second round in Paris.

“Obviously he knows his body better than everyone, as do all the players out here. If they feel fit and ready to compete and mentally ready, they’re going to go play the tournament. They’re not just going to sit out for no reason, in my opinion,” Shelton continued. “So there’s got to be some sort of give.”

MORE: ‘Serious Consideration’ – Canadian Open Chiefs Send Urgent Warning to ATP With Jannik Sinner, Novak Djokovic Missing

When the star trio pulled out of the 2025 edition in Toronto, Shelton made the most of the opportunity to win his maiden Masters 1000 title. The American has already won three titles this season, but his form has lacked consistency. It remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success at the Montréal edition.

title: No alarm bells at Barcelona after young midfielder picks up knock during a friendly
description: Barcelona took on CE Europa in their first pre-season friendly, a closed-door affair meant to give Hansi Flick a chance to test out his players during a game.The German manager named a heavily La Masi...
fullText:
Barcelona took on CE Europa in their first pre-season friendly, a closed-door affair meant to give Hansi Flick a chance to test out his players during a game.

The German manager named a heavily La Masia-influenced starting line-up that saw the likes of Marc-Andre ter Stegen and Marc Casado come off the bench.

One player who did not play a single minute against Europa was Marc Bernal, with it later being revealed that he was suffering from some muscular discomfort.

Now, according to Javi Miguel in Diario AS, the 19-year-old has suffered a slight muscular overload and is following an individual programme in the gym while the club closely monitors his recovery.

Bernal’s knock not considered to be serious. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

There are no indications of a serious injury at this stage, but Barcelona want to prevent the problem from developing into something more significant.

Bernal did not feature in the recent friendly against Europa, with the coaching staff preferring caution over unnecessary risk. His workload will continue to be adjusted until he is ready to return to full team training.

That careful approach is understandable given his recent injury history. Bernal made an impressive start to his first-team career before suffering a serious cruciate ligament injury against Rayo Vallecano.

He returned last season and made quite an impression before suffering another ankle injury that saw his role diminish towards the end.

Bernal gearing up for an important season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Hansi Flick is likely to have an important role for Bernal to play in his team once the 2026-27 season begins.

Captain Frenkie de Jong faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines and, with Casado’s future uncertain, that likely means Gavi and Bernal are going to see a lot of minutes.

His composure in possession, physical presence and ability to receive the ball under pressure make him a natural fit for the role Barcelona need.

Thus, it is understandable that Barça are treating this overload with the utmost precaution.

The most important objective is not getting Bernal ready for the next friendly. It is ensuring he can handle an entire season without suffering another major setback.

A few cautious days in the gym could go a long way in setting him up for a breakthrough season, and it remains to be seen how long it takes before Bernal gets some minutes in pre-season.

title: Profiling Washington's defensive players on Shrine Bowl watch list
description: The Washington Huskies had 7 defensive or special teams players named to the East-West Shrine Bowl's annual summer watchlist earlier this week.
fullText:
Jedd Fisch's Washington Huskies have seven players from the defense or special teams on the East-West Shrine Bowl's annual Shrine Bowl 1000 watch list. Released earlier this week, inclusion on the list indicates a good chance that a player will be invited to either the Shrine Bowl or its competitor game, the Panini Senior Bowl, which will release its own watchlist later this summer.

Huskies defensive tackle Elinneus Davis, edge rusher Jacob Lane, linebackers Xe'ree Alexander and Jacob Manu, cornerback Emmanuel Karnley, safety Alex McLaughlin, and punter Hunter Green represented the defense and special teams on the list. Both are units Fisch overhauled going into the 2025 season, with Alexander, Manu, and McLaughlin all joining the team via the transfer portal before that year after Washington replaced outgoing defensive coordinator Steve Belichick with current coordinator Ryan Walters. Fisch also brought in special teams coordinator Chris Petrilli, although the results with the specialist group were more mixed in 2025. That led Washington to target Green, a Huskies legacy and former FCS All-American at Northern Colorado in 2024, in the transfer portal this offseason.

Davis has been a steadily ascending player and one of the few consistent presences on the Huskies' defensive line over the last three seasons, playing in 12 games as a redshirt freshman in 2024 and 13 with 10 starts last season. He was nearly unblockable during spring practices and could be in line for a huge year with a remade group including freshmen Derek Colman-Brusa, Tufanua Ionatana Umu-Cais, and JD Hill and transfers Darin Conley, DeSean Watts, and Kai McClendon. As a fourth-year player, Davis will also be eligible to return to Montlake in 2027.

Lane was ranked just behind Davis in Washington's class of 2023 as the 14th and 15th-best composite recruits in that cycle. Considering how much the top of that class has atrophied - 6th-ranked Rashid Williams is the highest-rated player remaining on Washington's roster, and just three of the top ten recruits from that cycle remain on Montlake - the fact that the Huskies have three players (Lane, Davis, and center Landen Hatchett) from the class on the Shrine Bowl watchlist is impressive.

Lane would be off to the NFL one way or another had the NCAA not changed its eligibility rules in June, which will allow the in-state Emerald Ridge standout to return to Washington in 2027 if he doesn't build on his first season as a full-time starter to his satisfaction.

Alexander may very well end up being somewhat of a surprise to Huskies fans when the NFL draft rolls around, as his feedback in league circles seems borderline hyperbolic for a player who will be a part-time starter for Washington this season. But all of the Huskies' linebackers will play a ton this year, and a defensive MVP honor from the LA Bowl allowed Alexander to finish his first season on Montlake with a flourish. The UCF transfer also has the benefit of arriving at the right time: the NFL has coveted players who can switch between off-ball linebacker and edge rusher in recent seasons. Alexander, like Lane, has a fifth season available due to the NCAA rule change, but he may find his middle-round NFL projection more enticing than returning to start on a full-time basis next to Zaydrius Rainey-Sale.

Manu only played five games last season as Washington tried to slow-play his arrival in the hopes that this summer's NCAA rule changes would come in the middle of last season, which would've allowed Manu to be fully active last year without sacrificing his ability to return in 2026. Instead, Huskies fans only caught glimpses of what the Arizona transfer is capable of, but his spring session this offseason should have those same fans eager to see what he can do without Fisch assigning an assistant to make sure the senior doesn't trot out of the tunnel with his pads on every week. Listed at 5-foot-9, Manu has an uphill battle to make the league, but his tenacity and competitive spirit should be enough to get his foot in the door. An invite to an event like the Shrine Bowl, where players get more face time with NFL personnel, would undoubtedly be extremely helpful for him.

Karnley spent the 2023 season with Fisch and defensive backs coach John Richardson at Arizona before electing to stay in Tucson when the staff headed north to Seattle. His performance as a redshirt freshman was good enough to get him a transfer portal commitment to Miami, but he left after the spring and landed at Virginia, where he broke up 8 passes and intercepted another before reuniting with Fisch and Richardson for his fourth college football season. He'll be tasked with filling the shoes of Tacario Davis and Ephesians Prysock, who were both drafted into the NFL after locking down the boundaries for the Huskies last year. He doesn’t have the same size profile as those two or sophomore starter Dylan Robinson at "only" 6-foot, but his familiarity with the staff and proven production around the country bode well for his role on Montlake.

🔟 Huskies selected to @ShrinersBowl 2027 Shriners Children’s East-West Bowl 1000 watchlist. pic.twitter.com/C5y3EfpMMV

— Washington Football (@UW_Football) July 23, 2026

McLaughlin is a former FCS Freshman All-American at Northern Arizona who the Washington staff brought in last season to help bolster the safety position with Walters turning to more three-safety looks on the back end of the Huskies defense. Few FCS-to-FBS transfer portal additions were more successful, as McLaughlin earned honorable mention All-Big Ten and team defensive MVP honors after starting every game for Washington. With the size to play in the box but the coverage ability to hang with just about anybody in coverage, McLaughlin has the same benefit of Alexander of potentially entering the NFL right as their skillsets are held in the highest esteem. He is a perfect fit for the NFL’s pivot to bigger nickel and “apex” players like Kyle Hamilton of the Baltimore Ravens and Nick Emmanwori of the Seattle Seahawks.

Green told the media during spring practice that his aim is to win the Ray Guy Award this season, and he should be among the preseason favorites to take home the award. That could also roll forward into being one of the few punters drafted in the 2027 class. The first step in any of that will be transforming Washington’s punt unit, which struggled in just about every metric last season with Luke Dunne handling duties. Green, however, was No. 6 in the FBS in punting average, which should give Washington’s standout defense more opportunities to keep the Huskies in games.

Washington begins fall camp in early August, with the Shrine Bowl kicking off the NFL draft cycle at the end of January.

title: Report: Cavaliers’ LeBron Chances Took Major Blow After Mobley Trade Decision
description: While the NBA world is still bumping with emotion over the LeBron James to Philadelphia 76ers news, the Cleveland Cavaliers are still processing what hit them.Not only did James say no to a storybook reunion, but he joined the conference rival instead. So what led to the four-time league MVP passing on a reunion when […] The post Report: Cavaliers’ LeBron Chances Took Major Blow After Mobley Trade Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
While the NBA world is still bumping with emotion over the LeBron James to Philadelphia 76ers news, the Cleveland Cavaliers are still processing what hit them.

Not only did James say no to a storybook reunion, but he joined the conference rival instead. So what led to the four-time league MVP passing on a reunion when many were convinced that was his best path forward?

According to NBA insider Brett Siegel, the Cavs decision to not trade for Jaylen Brown likely played a major role in James saying no to Cleveland.

“The issue of the Cavaliers not making any moves to improve their roster, specifically not pursuing Jaylen Brown when Boston was making him available, also clearly influenced James’ decision. If Cleveland was willing to part ways with Evan Mobley in a deal for Brown, that would’ve weighed heavily in LeBron’s mind, but this is simply a hypothetical game at this juncture.”

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 22: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics attempts a shot against LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of their game at Crypto.com Arena on February 22, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luiza Moraes/Getty Images)

The Cavs thought they were sitting pretty by not making any moves. They wanted to preserve all the flexibility needed to add James to the roster and, perhaps, pay him significantly more than what competing teams could offer.

Instead, they may have been watching their chances to land The King quickly fade away as James held back to see which teams were making big moves.

The Sixers pulled the trigger. They landed Brown, the 29-year-old perennial All-Star, from the Boston Celtics in a stunning, and rather lopsided, trade.

Clearly, that move caught James’ eyes and ears. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the Sixers did not register on James’ radar until they acquired Brown.

“Philadelphia, I’m telling you was not even on this radar, was not in the pool of candidates until Bob Myers went out and got Jaylen Brown that changed the equation,” Charania said on ESPN’s First Take Friday morning following James’ move to the Sixers. “The Sixers got on the map and from there it became for LeBron James now almost four weeks of deliberation with LeBron James, Rich Paul, that inner circle there and his family, eventually.”

HOUSTON, TEXAS – MARCH 16: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the National Anthem prior to the game against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center on March 16, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images)

The day after the James news was announced, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst laid out the three biggest reasons why James chose Philadelphia over Cleveland.

“In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron’s choice, the front office not making a deal for (Jaylen) Brown and the Cavs’ roster not featuring (Darius) Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture,” Windhorst wrote.

Garland, James’ fellow Klutch Sports client, was moved to the Los Angeles Clippers for James Harden in a trade in February. Windhorst believes the Cavs’ decision to move Garland, with whom James has a strong relationship, is another reason why James didn’t return to Cleveland.

If that is also true, then it boils down to this: the Cavs lost James months before he ever signed with the 76ers. The Garland trade in February started the slide, and not making a move for Brown this summer became the final blow.

title: ‘They’ve Just Had His Number’ — CFB Analyst Reveals Georgia HC Kirby Smart’s Toughest Road Game in 2026 Season
description: Kirby Smart’s Georgia enters the 2026 season as the favorite in the Southeastern Conference as he leads a roster stocked with elite talent, like quarterback Gunner Stockton. However, the Bulldogs face a demanding road schedule, with difficult matchups against Alabama and Ole Miss expected to test their championship aspirations.
fullText:
Kirby Smart’s Georgia enters the 2026 season as the favorite in the Southeastern Conference as he leads a roster stocked with elite talent, like quarterback Gunner Stockton. However, the Bulldogs face a demanding road schedule, with difficult matchups against Alabama and Ole Miss expected to test their championship aspirations.

Georgia has plenty of reasons to be wary of Ole Miss after the Rebels ended the Bulldogs’ 2025 season with a 39-34 win in the Sugar Bowl. Even after Lane Kiffin departed just before the College Football Playoff, Pete Golding led Ole Miss to an incredible comeback, overcoming a 21-12 halftime deficit to eliminate Georgia.

Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss starred in that win, completing 30 of 46 passes for 362 yards and 2 touchdowns. Unless Smart can devise a better strategy this time around, Georgia could be headed for another difficult night when it visits Oxford on Nov. 7.

That concern is shared by much of Georgia’s fan base, and DawgsHQ’s Rusty Mansell also said he believes most Bulldogs fans see Ole Miss as the team’s toughest road test of the upcoming season.

“I would say if you set 100 UGA fans right here, I bet you 85 would say Ole Miss,” Mansell said in “That SEC Podcast.”

However, Mansell pointed out that he personally can’t get over the Alabama road trip.

“For whatever reason, I’m not over that Alabama point yet because of what they have done to Georgia, particularly under Kirby,” Mansell said. “You know what I mean? They’ve just had his number.

“He did have a very impressive win in the SEC Championship. It’s a bit like he goes to Tuscaloosa every year. They’re like, ‘Kirby, guess what? You’re going back to Tuscaloosa.’ He’s been like three times. I’m like, ‘My God.’ And they’ve been to Athens once. And then Ty Simpson lit him up. So, I would say until Kirby goes down and Georgia wins that game in Alabama, that momentum they’ve had would be over.”

MORE: College Football Playoff Predictor

Smart owns just a 2-7 career record against Alabama, but he finally broke through with a 28-7 win over the Crimson Tide in last season’s SEC Championship Game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. It marked Georgia’s most decisive win over Alabama since its 21-0 win on Oct. 2, 1976.

However, Georgia still has something to prove in Tuscaloosa. The Bulldogs will travel to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Oct. 10, where Smart has yet to win as Georgia’s head coach. The venue is one of only three SEC stadiums where he remains winless, and it’s also a place where the Bulldogs have not celebrated a victory since 2007. That history makes this year’s trip another big hurdle for Smart and his team.

title: Fronts on the left, rears on the right! Massive blunder hampers Thiim
description: A costly mistake by Pirelli made the Aston Martin of mid-season champion Nicki Thiim practically undriveable: How it happened and what the consequences were
fullText:
Saturday at Oschersleben was already a disaster for Nicki Thiim with 18th on the grid and 12th at the finish, which caused a lot of frustration. But on Sunday, things got even worse for the DTM mid-season champion: In qualifying, where the Aston Martin pilot only managed 19th despite an adjusted Balance of Performance (BoP), tire manufacturer Pirelli made a grave mistake.

"This morning, to put it professionally, Pirelli put the front tires on the rear rims - and vice versa," Thiim reveals. "I'm glad it's over, to be honest - a weekend to completely write off."

Already on Saturday he had "no chance" - and today "Pirelli really messed up the whole day," says the Dane, who managed to salvage 13th place in the race. "A mistake like this simply should not happen at this level. This obviously has a big impact on our championship. It is not the team's fault," he says, defending his crew at ran.de.

In fact, such a faux pas has massive implications for performance: Thiim had both rear tires mounted on the right and both front tires on the left - and they differ in their dimensions. The rear tires are one centimeter wider and have a two-centimeter larger diameter than the front tires.

"The problem is that the tires differ in height and rolling circumference. If I have tires from the rear on the front axle, my whole car no longer works. My rolling circumference is different, I have different wheel speeds," explains Mario Schuhbauer, who acts as DTM sporting director for the Comtoyou team, at ran.de.

"At first I thought it was a puncture," Thiim initially suspected a tyre problem. No wonder, as Schuhbauer clarifies: "The car is crooked." And there are further problems: "The ABS system no longer works. My differential gets too hot because I have different speeds at the wheels."

In fact, the sensors on the left side of the vehicle registered a wheel speed several km/h higher than on the right. The balance of the car was also completely shifted by the error and the electronics no longer functioned as usual, which is why the ABS eventually failed. The fact that the differential reached its limit and later broke was also audible. It had to be replaced after qualifying.

Nevertheless, it is impressive that despite the problem in qualifying, Thiim only lost 0.773 seconds to Thomas Preining's pole time - and above all was 0.124 seconds faster than teammate Nicolas Baert. "Nicki did a really good job with the problem - normally you could just stop right there," says Schuhbauer.

But how could Pirelli make such a mistake? And should the team have realized something was wrong? "It cannot only be Pirelli's fault," says former DTM champion Maximilian Gotz at ran.de. "The mechanics have the tires in their hands. They have to see that something is not right." One must "also hold the team accountable to check everything so that this does not happen."

The teams hand over their four rims to Pirelli at the track and pick them up later with tires mounted. While these are fitted with a barcode and registered in the system, it is not apparent from this whether they are front or rear tires.

Theoretically, the crew could have noticed visually that the tire and the rim did not match, but according to Schuhbauer, the error was "unfortunately not ours." Nevertheless, he knows that Pirelli did not act with intent either. "We are all human, it can happen," says the former SSR Performance team boss.

Due to the unfortunate faux pas, the Comtoyou team was allowed to replace all four tires that were used in qualifying and were no longer in good condition with a completely new set before the race. The team submitted a request, which was approved by the technical delegate.

Thanks to a good strategy, Thiim, who was allowed to start from 18th on the grid due to Ben Dorr's grid penalty, managed to move up to 13th place. "The crew put on the best pit stop of the day," he says, referring to the tire changes, which were completed in 6.2 and 6.1 seconds respectively. "I just love this crew."

In the overall standings, the mid-season champion has lost the lead due to Maro Engel's two podium finishes and is now the first pursuer, 21 points behind the Winward Mercedes driver.

title: Explained: McLaren's view of Oscar Piastri's explosive F1 Hungarian GP radio outburst
description: McLaren says it understands Oscar Piastri's team radio outburst during Formula 1's Hungarian Grand Prix, but insists its pitstop strategy was the right call
fullText:
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella has explained the Formula 1 squad's thinking behind its second pitstop sequence in the Hungarian Grand Prix amid frustration from Oscar Piastri over his run-in with backmarker Carlos Sainz.

In their quest to deliver a first grand prix win of the season, both Piastri and team-mate Lando Norris showed frustration in the heat of the moment, belying the sense of urgency for the reigning world champions to gain a foothold in the 2026 campaign.

Early season dominator Mercedes had been challenged by a resurgent Ferrari and its innovative, heavily upgraded car. But last year's dominant team had started 2026 on the back foot, so when a significant floor upgrade finally appeared to put McLaren in the mix, neither Norris nor Piastri needed any further encouragement to put it to good use.

Having done the heavy lifting by putting the MCL40 on pole, Norris couldn't afford any slip-ups on lap 1, but did exactly that by drifting offline through the dust in Turn 2. Having had a disappointing qualifying session, Piastri benefitted from penalties to take third on the grid and then swooped past Norris into the lead.

With overtaking extremely difficult without a tyre offset, that was Norris' afternoon ruined. And trying as he might to pressure Piastri into a mistake, Norris soon started hinting at how much quicker he could go in clear air. The situation continued until the second stint, when Norris was requested to be called in first.

"We can't," race engineer Will Joseph said. The usual etiquette is that the leading car gets pitstop priority and in this case Piastri had earned that right by passing Norris fair and square on lap one.

So when on lap 34 Hamilton, who had already pitted several laps earlier, was 25 seconds behind the leader and closing, the thinking at McLaren was that it needed to cover off the Ferrari as its main threat.

"When Hamilton pits, he is in condition to undercut the two McLarens, so we needed to respond," Stella explained. "Oscar was in the lead, and we thought that he was the right car to stop for that."

Piastri emerged ahead by four seconds, leaving Norris a gap to slot into as well. But through a combination of Piastri being baulked by Williams driver Sainz and Norris finding extra pace in clear air, Norris made a rare overcut work to take the lead, much to Piastri's chagrin.

"Get out of the f****** way you idiot, oh my god," Piastri raged at Sainz, before redirecting some of that frustration towards his own team when he saw his chance to win the race evaporate.

"Nice of you guys to factor that one in by the way, thanks," he said sarcastically.

Afterwards Piastri conceded that McLaren had no other choice but to pit him when he did, and that in the heat of the moment his racing driver brain had taken over from reason, hoping McLaren could somehow rectify the injustice.

"When Lando came out ahead, I knew I had no pace to go and attack him, so I knew my chances of winning the race were done from there," Piastri acknowledged. "I felt maybe the team could have not pitted Lando if it was a two-car race, but I know it's not a two-car race. They can't just not box Lando because of something out of his control and out of my control.

"From that side of things, it's fine. I was just very, very pissed off in the moment about what happened. Without getting crashed into, I would have been ahead of Lando still."

That's also how team principal Stella saw it, and he revealed that Piastri had explained his team radio comments afterwards.

"Immediately after the race, Oscar clarified that his comment was a comment in anger," Stella said when asked by Motorsport.com for comment.

"There were a couple of unfortunate episodes. Obviously, the most important is the fact that Oscar had a collision with a backmarker. And at the same time, once Lando was released, then his pace was simply mega. I think he found half a second per lap. And this pace meant that Lando could be ahead of Oscar."

He added: "I think Oscar understood it immediately. It's absolutely understandable that when you lead the race for almost half [of it], and then you see yourself losing the lead because of an episode with a backmarker, then you may have a moment and make a comment in anger, but there's absolutely no problem."

But Stella felt like Piastri had also "deserved an opportunity to try and win the race" by passing Norris at the start and then keeping him at bay.

"You constantly evaluate all the options," Stella added. "You can look at what's the way to score as many points for the team, but there's also a way to be consistent with the way we go racing.

"I think up until the time Oscar pitted, Oscar had gained the lead in a fair manner with the action in corner one and two, so he deserved an opportunity to try and win the race. On other tracks, probably Lando might have overtaken Oscar, but in this case it's difficult."

With McLaren the pick of the field on Sunday, swapping the order didn't prove necessary, but the team did try to calm a flying Norris down as it was managing various reliability concerns, both when he was chasing Piastri and when he was leading. Piastri's eventual retirement through a gearbox failure suggested that was not an unwise decision.

"The main thing with Lando is that we were managing a couple of things from a reliability point of view, so there was absolutely no need to use kerbs that we then instructed a couple of times quite explicitly," said Stella. "But Lando wasn't [trying to] prove anything. He was in the lead, in clean air, and he just had a lot of pace in hand."

In any case, McLaren's first race-winning outing of the season brought back memories of its many team order quandaries over last year's title winning campaign. With Piastri frustrated over his belated access to this weekend's floor upgrade, having been made to wait until FP3 on Saturday, Sunday's race only further put the spotlight on McLaren's fairness mantra.

title: ‘This Is Pathetic,’ ‘Always a Victim’ — NFL World Rips Ryan Clark for Crying After Getting Fired by ESPN

fullText:

title: Nathaniel Hackett's "definitely a rookie" remark about Jeremiyah Love is getting overblown
description: We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem.
fullText:
We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem. But certain supposedly controversial comments aren't really as big of a deal as some may interpret them to be.

Case in point: Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett is catching some heat for comments he made on Saturday about rookie running back Jeremiyah Love.

"He's definitely a rookie, and — as we've talked about," Hackett said. "And he'll keep growing every single day. I'm very excited for him. All those guys. Not just him."

The broader context has to be considered, especially since Hackett specifically added "as we've talked about."

Earlier in the session, Hackett addressed the challenges that first-year players face when training camp opens. The question related to the things that are different for rookies.

"Everything you can imagine," Hackett said. "I mean, coming to this league is — I mean, just the speed is so different. You talk about the speed, being in a new building. . . . [I]t's a whole new environment. New people to work with, and definitely new playbooks that are very, very intricate. Due to the fact of all the things that we see and all the different — I mean, just our defense out there. I mean, you get almost everything and more. Which is great, because it helps you for the season, but for a young player to have to be able to adjust and learn just basic system and then apply it to different defenses. It takes some time. So heads are spinning right now, especially after two days, but I think it'll just get better and better. That's the goal."

Hackett wasn't dismissing or minimizing Love. He's a rookie. Like the rest of the rookies. Everything is different. Everything is new. "Heads are spinning," as Hackett said.

Training camp is the time to slow, and eventually to stop, the spinning. They have plenty of time to get Love ready to go. For now, after only two days, he's beginning the adjustment.

That's all it means. Which makes the comment not nearly as alarming as some are making it out to be.

title: Corey Seager takes live BP for first time since back injury again sidelined Rangers shortstop
description: Corey Seager took live batting practice Sunday for the first time since the Texas Rangers shortstop was sidelined by a back injury for the second time this season on July 1.  Seager finished the session with a home run and was planning to take live BP again Monday before what would appear to be a minor league rehab assignment.  The two-time World Series MVP played two games in the minors in early June when he was returning from a three-week absence because of lower back inflammation.
fullText:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Corey Seager took live batting practice Sunday for the first time since the Texas Rangers shortstop was sidelined by a back injury for the second time this season on July 1.

Seager finished the session with a home run and was planning to take live BP again Monday before what would appear to be a minor league rehab assignment.

The two-time World Series MVP played two games in the minors in early June when he was returning from a three-week absence because of lower back inflammation. Seager spent two more weeks on the injured list in June after getting a concussion.

“It's just tough to mimic some in-game stuff,” manager Skip Schumaker said of a possible rehab stint. “It's always up to the player. Because he missed so much time, we're going to discuss it. Looked like today was really good. See what it feels like tomorrow, and then we'll discuss the rehab assignment.”

Seager was removed from a game at Toronto in the first inning on June 30 because of back discomfort. The five-time All-Star is almost certain to play his fewest games since joining the Rangers in 2022.

Seager has been limited to 51 games in what has been the worst season of his career. He is hitting .182 with 10 home runs and 25 RBIs. Seager was in an 0-for-27 slide, the worst of his career, when he was sidelined by the back injury the first time.

After returning from the concussion, Seager played in three games before his back flared up. He wasn't ready to say he had a better handle on dealing with a balky back for a second time.

“I would love to tell you yes, but backs are not what you want,” Seager said.

The Rangers also are hopeful for the return soon of a pair of left-handers who haven't pitched in the big leagues since 2024.

Jordan Montgomery underwent the second elbow reconstruction surgery of his career last year when he was with Arizona. He joined the Diamondbacks after playing a key role for the Rangers when they won the World Series in 2023. Montgomery rejoined the Rangers on a one-year contract this year.

Cody Bradford, who had elbow surgery in June 2025, made 34 appearances in 21 starts over his first two big league seasons with the Rangers before getting shut down during spring training last year. Bradford also had a strong showing in the World Series when he was a rookie.

title: Crowds line streets to cheer on football's brightest young prospects
description: Thousands of young footballers have paraded through the streets of Coleraine to cheering crowds.
fullText:
Thousands of people have cheered on young footballers from across the globe taking part in the opening parade of a prestigious youth football tournament in Coleraine.

The Budget Energy SuperCupNI, formerly the Milk Cup, has brought together 1,200 players from boys' and girls' teams, including clubs such as Manchester United, Liverpool, Rangers and Celtic.

Teams have travelled from countries as far away as Mexico, Japan, Norway, the USA and the United Arab Emirates to play in more than 150 fixtures in the six-day tournament.

SuperCupNI has a long history of showcasing some of football's brightest young talents, with former participants including Marcus Rashford, Sergio Busquets and Mats Hummels.

Desert Empire Surf have travelled all the way from Florida in the United States for the tournament.

Head coach Hugo Chaparro said his team, who are competing in the girls' premier section, cannot wait to get started and test themselves against some of the biggest clubs in world football.

Their opening fixture is on Monday, when they travel to Limavady to take on Liverpool, who are competing in the division for the first time.

Desert Empire Surf will then play IL Heming from Norway before facing Manchester United in Newtownabbey.

Chaparro said the experience gives young players the opportunity to test themselves against different styles of football, experience other cultures and create memories that will last a lifetime.

For players like Katina and Keira, they cannot wait to play in the tournament against some of the top players.

They said despite the tough group, they believe they can compete at the top level.

Former Northern Ireland footballer Chris Brunt officially opened the event, leading the parade through Coleraine town centre before declaring the tournament officially open at the Showgrounds, home of Northern Ireland Football League side Coleraine FC.

The former West Bromwich Albion captain, who won 65 caps for Northern Ireland, previously played in the tournament's Elite Section in 2003.

Brunt said he has fond memories of playing in the tournament.

He remembers facing a young Brazil side featuring future Manchester City midfielder Fernandinho, while playing alongside future Northern Ireland internationals Steven Davis, Michael McGovern, Dean Shiels and Sammy Clingan at Windsor Park in front of 4,000 spectators.

Brunt, who enjoyed a distinguished playing career spanning almost two decades and now works in coaching and player development at West Brom, said it was a "real honour" to open the tournament, describing the SuperCupNI as a competition every young footballer aspired to play in.

He said that throughout his career he had played with and against players from all over the world, and that whenever the tournament came up in conversation, people always spoke highly about the experience.

The tournament was the brainchild of Coleraine's Victor Leonard, local youth football administrator Jim Weir and former Northern Ireland and Celtic midfielder Bertie Peacock, who first met in December 1981 to lay the foundations for an international youth football tournament.

First staged in 1983, the competition was originally known as the Northern Ireland Cup before being renamed the Milk Cup following sponsorship from Northern Ireland's dairy industry.

Motherwell won the inaugural tournament by defeating hosts Coleraine, and the competition has grown significantly over the decades. Now known as SuperCupNI, it annually welcomes thousands of young players from around the world.

SuperCupNI typically follows the conclusion of another high-profile youth football competition, the O'Neills Foyle Cup, which held its traditional team parade in Londonderry earlier this month.

Games took place across the north west of Northern Ireland and also across the border in County Donegal in the Republic of Ireland.

title: Ana Capeta goal secures Bianconere win over Como Women
description: The Juventus Women’s First Team beat Como Women 2-1 in Vinovo to secure their second pre-season friendly victory of the summer.Following their win against Servette and the 5-0 victory over Aarau on ...
fullText:
The Juventus Women’s First Team beat Como Women 2-1 in Vinovo to secure their second pre-season friendly victory of the summer.

Following their win against Servette and the 5-0 victory over Aarau on Saturday, the 25th, the Bianconere capped off a very productive weekend of training and secured a win against a team they’ll face in the upcoming Serie A Women season, thanks to goals by Emma Stolen Godo in the first half and Ana Capeta in stoppage time of the second half.

It was a lively start and, after just six minutes, Como Women took the lead: Linnea Borbye found space down the centre for Veronica Bernardi, who found herself one-on-one with Larissa Rusek and made it 1-0.

Juventus’s response comes shortly afterwards. In the 10th minute, a swift counter-attack orchestrated by Annamaria Serturini set up Alba Redondo for a shot: her effort was parried, but Stolen Godo was on hand for the rebound, firing a powerful right-footed shot under the crossbar to make it 1–1.

The Bianconere tried to take control of the game, whilst Como posed a threat mainly on the counter-attack. As the first half drew to a close, the score remained level.

In the second half, Juventus dominated possession for long spells, but Como were not sitting back and launched dangerous forays towards the Bianconere goal, such as the one in the 42nd minute, when Abi Brighton made a decisive intervention, clearing a tricky situation in her own box with superb timing after Nadine Nischler had beaten Rusek.

Just as the match seemed destined to end in a draw, the decisive moment arrived. In the second minute of stoppage time, Eva Schatzer played a through ball to Capeta, who shielded the ball, won the one-on-one with the defender and, from a very tight angle, found the right corner to beat Rumba and seal the final 2–1 victory.

This marks Juventus' third consecutive victory in pre-season, following a useful friendly designed to build up match fitness and continue their development ahead of the start of the new season.

title: Steelers’ Will Howard earns support from unlikeliest ally
description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard received support from longtime critic Mark Madden.
fullText:
Miracles do happen, as Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard received support from the unlikeliest of all places — longtime critic Mark Madden.

Despite once calling Howard a “practice squad lifer,” the ever-outspoken Madden revealed on a new podcast episode of 105.9 The X that he’s switching his stance to support the young quarterback.

“It’s my big switcheroo regarding the Steelers’ quarterback position,” Madden said. “This is way out of left field, but I am jumping on the Will Howard bandwagon. I don’t believe he’s the long-term answer. But I know for sure that Mason Rudolph ain’t the long-term answer. And I also believe that Mason Rudolph can’t win enough if [Aaron] Rodgers gets hurt and the backup has to play. I would have no problem keeping Will Howard as the No. 2. In fact, I now believe it’s a good idea.”

Madden continued, saying that Rudolph would only be the preferable option if Rodgers needed to miss only a series or two during a game, but Howard is the better choice for the Steelers’ future.

Honestly, Madden’s comments are extremely surprising because the longtime Pittsburgh voice has spent so much time bashing Howard. But it’s still a welcome change as training camp approaches.

title: Browns offensive line remains uncertain despite all the roster additions
description: Bggest need after the 2025 season for the Cleveland Browns roster was on the OLine. Did free agency, draft do enough?
fullText:
The NFL season is slowly approaching, as teams are beginning to report to training camp. For the Cleveland Browns, the rookies have already reported, with veterans required in town early this week. The team has undergone multiple changes this offseason; the most noticeable is the offensive line.

The Browns have essentially replaced the entire offensive line from last season, with two rookies potentially starting. The free agency acquisitions, signing guards Elgton Jenkins (who could also play center) and Zion Johnson, as well as trading for tackle Tytus Howard, were all brought in to help bolster this line. With the moves that Cleveland made to improve the offensive line, the question everyone asked was whether the team did enough to improve one of the weakest offensive lines in football last season.

It’s not an understatement to say that many of the Browns offensive problems last year stemmed from lackluster offensive line play. With instability at the tackle spots and deteriorating play on the interior, Cleveland’s offensive line struggles were more of an issue than people want to admit; blaming quarterbacks and coaches is way more fun.

Browns GM Andrew Berry is known for attacking position groups that are the weakest. Berry has done this multiple times during his tenure in Cleveland, and this year he’s done it with the offensive line. In terms of the tackle spots, trading for Howard was the first domino that fell. Howard was the lone bright spot on a struggling Houston Texans offensive line and brings versatility, as he can play both guard and tackle. The same can be said for Jenkins. Before tearing his ACL, Jenkins was a two-time Pro Bowler with the Green Bay Packers. Jenkins is primarily a guard, but the Packers chose to move him to center this past season; while the results were less than ideal, that is the role he could play in Cleveland as well. When healthy, Jenkins has proven he can be a quality starter.

The team’s biggest splash this free agency was signing Johnson, who also played on a struggling offensive line with the Los Angeles Chargers, and is likely going to start at the left guard position.

Spencer Fano, who the Browns drafted in the first round of the 2026 NFL draft, is the cornerstone of this offensive line. Fano, who was one of the top prospects in his class, has the versatility to be kicked inside if necessary, but it’s likely he will be the team’s starting left tackle for the future. Parker Brailsford, who the team drafted in the fifth round, could potentially start at center for the team. Austin Barber was also drafted, adding another young tackle option.

On paper, this unit is better than last season’s group. Versatility is what stands out for the archetype of players that the Browns acquired. Multiple players that can play different positions. However, it’s a valid question if Cleveland did enough to improve the unit. Center Tyler Linderbaum was a highly coveted offensive lineman in free agency, but he chose to sign with the Las Vegas Raiders. Linderbaum would’ve made sense for the Browns due to his familiarity with current head coach Todd Monken and his scheme, but his price tag would’ve been too hefty for the team to pay, and it would’ve crippled the rest of the unit in terms of paying for other players.

Overall, this unit looks improved, but time will tell if the moves made in free agency and in the draft will pay dividends.

title: Cole Sands returns at good time for Twins bullpen
description: The Twins got good news Sunday when reliever Cole Sands was activated from the injured list, where he had been since May 2 because of a forearm strain. “It’s a good return for us, a guy we planned on him being a big part of our bullpen early in the year as missed significant time,” manager Derek Shelton said. “So, to get him back is nice.” Sands, 29, was one of the few bullpen veterans left ...
fullText:
The Twins got good news Sunday when reliever Cole Sands was activated from the injured list, where he had been since May 2 because of a forearm strain.

“It’s a good return for us, a guy we planned on him being a big part of our bullpen early in the year as missed significant time,” manager Derek Shelton said. “So, to get him back is nice.”

Sands, 29, was one of the few bullpen veterans left after last July’s trade deadline, when Minnesota traded away Louis Varland, Jhoan Duran, Griffin Jax, Danny Coulombe and Brock Stewart. He hasn’t pitched since April, allowing six earned runs on 12 hits and four walks in 12 appearances.

He struck out 11 in 11⅔ innings and had one save.

Coles arrived in time to take the roster spot of Michael Peredes, who suffered a Grade 2 oblique strain while warming up for what was to be the first part of a bullpen on Saturday against the A’s.

“So, not days; it’s gonna be weeks,” Shelton said. “So, we’ll figure it out as we get more into this. But overall, not the greatest of news. But with the way he responded in the bullpen, and the way he responded afterwards, we kind of thought this was the case.”

With Coles back, the Twins now have four relief pitchers on the injured list: Peredes, Garrett Acton (shoulder strain), Anthony Banda (lat strain) and Marco Raya (shoulder impingement).

Rookie left-hander Connor Prielipp was reinstated from the 15-day IL (blister) and started Sunday’s series final against the A’s. To make room on the active roster, the Twins optioned reliever Jack Anderson back to St. Paul.

Right-hander Joe Ryan missed a regular start this weekend for what Shelton on Saturday called arm fatigue. Instead, he threw a bullpen session on Saturday.

In his last start, his first since pitching an inning in the All-Star Game on July 13, Ryan allowed a franchise-high six home runs in a 10-6 loss at Cleveland on July 22. He is slotted to pitch Wednesday against Kansas City at Target Field.

“After the bullpen yesterday, I talked to him last night after the game and he was in a good spot,” Shelton said. “We just wanted to make sure we backed it up to give him enough rest to do it.”

Shelton said Taj Bradley will pitch Tuesday and that Bailey Ober is set for the third game of the series against the Royals.

title: Magomed Zaynukov takes aim at Ilia Topuria after UFC debut win
description: Mocking Ilia Topuria was the first item on Magomed "Chanco" Zaynukov's list after winning his UFC debut in Abu Dhabi.
fullText:
Magomed Zaynukov's first order of business after winning his anticipated UFC Fight Night 282 debut was to take aim at former lightweight champion Ilia Topuria.

Zaynukov (9-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC) lived up to the hype on Saturday in Abu Dhabi when he put on a scintillating striking performance en route to a unanimous decision win over fellow octagon newcomer Damian Rzepecki (10-1 MMA, 0-1 UFC).

Once his hand was raised and Daniel Cormier joined him in the octagon for the post-fight interview, Zaynukov immediately mentioned Topuria (17-1 MMA, 9-1 UFC) and noted how Rzepecki had spent a portion of his camp with "El Matador" prior to his UFC Freedom 250 title loss to Justin Gaethje.

“Hey Ilia Topuria! I just wanted to make sure to come out here and do my work," Zaynukov said to Cormier through an interpreter. "He was saying he was from the team of Ilia Topuria. Well guess what? I come from the school of Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. We do not care who we fight. We’ll take anyone!”

There was also a post-fight tweet from a fake Zaynukov account on X calling Topuria a "quitter" that picked up some traction, but the account has since been suspended and removed from the social media platform.

The in-cage comments were enough to show Zaynukov's intentions however, and after Topuria spent several months targeting former 155-pound titleholder Islam Makhachev and pursuing that match, it's clear there's some unresolved tension between the two camps.

Could Zaynukov eventually work his way into position to fight Topuria? It remains to be seen how quickly the promotion will try to escalate him up the rankings after his debut win.

fullText:
Tadej Pogačar has done it again. The Slovenian cyclist has won the Tour de France for the third consecutive year. He's won the race five times in his career.

Pogačar has now tied France's Jacques Anquetil and Bernard Hinault, Eddy Merckx of Belgium and Spain's Miguel Indurain for most Tour de France championships at five. Indurain remains the only cyclist to win the race five consecutive times, from 1991 to 1995.

(Lance Armstrong won seven straight Tours de France from 1999 to 2005, but the International Cycling Union stripped him of those titles in 2012 due to alleged use of illegal performance-enhancing drugs, blood transfusions and schemes to deceive testing authorities.)

title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, becomes first player to achieve unique T20I feat before turning 16
description: The left-handed opener achieved the feat during the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare on Sunday, scoring 81 off 48 balls to lead India to 192/5 after they elected to bat first.
fullText:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi continued to rewrite records as the 15-year-old became only the first player in men's international cricket to register multiple scores of 50 or more before turning 16.

The left-handed opener achieved the feat during the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare on Sunday, scoring 81 off 48 balls to lead India to 192/5 after they elected to bat first.

Only Nepal's Kushal Malla had previously recorded a 50-plus score in men's internationals before turning 16. Sooryavanshi has now gone one better with two such scores to his name.

50-plus scores before turning 16 in Men’s internationals

2 - Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (India)

On a pitch that offered assistance to the bowlers, Sooryavanshi showed a different side to his batting. He began cautiously, scoring 11 runs from his first 10 balls and 26 from his first 20 deliveries before bringing up his second T20I fifty in 31 balls.

His innings still included some of the strokeplay that has become his trademark. He drove Brad Evans straight down the ground for four off a yorker and later launched off-spinner Sikandar Raza for a 102-metre six. He also reverse-swept Wesley Madhevere for a boundary.

While Sooryavanshi settled in, opening partner Abhishek Sharma's lean run continued. Abhishek edged Blessing Muzarabani to wicketkeeper Tadi Marumani for two, extending his sequence of low scores. His last six innings have produced 10, 16, 3, 1, 8 and 2, dating back to the third T20I against England in Nottingham last month.

Sooryavanshi then added 75 runs for the second wicket with Ishan Kishan, who made 29, before sharing a 50-run partnership with captain Shreyas Iyer, who scored 27.

The youngster looked set for a century before Wesley Madhevere dismissed him. Brad Evans completed a catch at long-off to end his innings on 81.

India could not maintain the same scoring rate after the departures of Sooryavanshi and Shreyas. The middle order added only 47 runs in the final five overs, with Rinku Singh's 25 off 14 balls helping India move closer to the 200-run mark.

India finished on 192/5, a total that could prove competitive on a surface offering help to the bowlers.

title: Madison's Jerry Kelly wins Senior Open after clutch bunker shot on 18
description: Jerry Kelly held off a trio of challengers to win the 2026 ISPS Handa Senior Open, his third major title on the PGA Champions Tour.
fullText:
Madison's Jerry Kelly held off a trio of challengers to win the 2026 ISPS Handa Senior Open  at Gleneagles in Auchterarder, Perthshire, Scotland on Sunday, July 27.

Up one stoke entering the final hole, Kelly saved his best for last with a sensational bunker shot that set up a short birdie putt on the par-5 18th to finish 10-under and win the final senior major tournament of the year by two strokes. over Matt Gogel, Cameron Percy and Darren Finchardt.

Percy had a six-foot putt for birdie at 18 that could have created some nerves for Kelly, forcing him to make his 4-footer after his fabulous bunker shot, but Percy's putt went wide of the hole, giving Kelly two putts to clinch his win. He only needed one. Kelly and Percy were tied for the lead heading into the final round.

"Wow.... I've always loved coming to the home of golf," Kelly said after receiving the trophy "It always brings incredible warmth and joy to my heart,"

Kelly shot his third straight 2-under par round of 68 after an opening 66 on July 23. Gogel made a huge charge with a a 7-under 63 on the final 18, but Kelly continued his steady and consistent play on the back nine to keep the lead. He did not have a bogey after the 11th hole and capped his victory with a clinching fourth birdie of the round on 18.

This is the third senior major title for Kelly. He also won the 2020 and 2022 Senior Players Championships. Kelly has 13 titles on the PGA Tour Champions.

title: The error that led to Lewis Hamilton's Hungarian GP penalty
description: The seven-time F1 world champion went over the pitlane speed limit by just 0.1km/h during the Hungarian GP
fullText:
Formula 1 is a game of fine margins and there is no greater example than the five-second penalty Lewis Hamilton received at the Hungarian Grand Prix for pitlane speeding.

The seven-time world champion was second at the Hungaroring before pitting on lap 56 under virtual safety car conditions due to a gearbox failure forcing Oscar Piastri to stop before Turn 4.

It was a costly stop for two reasons: one, it led to Hamilton dropping behind Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli who didn’t pit and, two, what the Ferrari driver did at pit exit caused his penalty.

Ferrari revealed that the Briton pressed the pitlane speed limiter button too early, causing him to go just 0.1km/h above the limit, which dropped him to fifth in the classification behind team-mate Charles Leclerc after crossing the line in fourth.

“This isn’t a good result at all,” Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur told Canal+. “We can’t be satisfied with this. We made too many mistakes today, beginning with the two starts.

“Then we lost a position on the track to Verstappen and we made mistakes during the pitstops. The pit limiter [was] released too early. In the end, it’s not good.”

Sunday just added to a long list of penalties Hamilton has received across the past three race weekends, starting with Silverstone where he suffered an additional five seconds for a false start.

The 41-year-old was also penalised five seconds for contact with George Russell at Les Combes on lap one of the Belgian Grand Prix, the day Ferrari was also fined for an unsafe release on Hamilton who knocked down a mechanic in the pitlane.

Hungary qualifying then saw Hamilton impede Piastri at Turn 1 - the Ferrari driver called it a “communication error” - resulting in a three-place grid drop to start fifth and not second.

When these incidents were put to Vasseur, he replied: “It's difficult to put all the penalties in the same basket.

“For me, the accident with Russell, it's a race incident. If he has to do it again, I would ask him to do exactly the same, because he can't go on the kerb.

“Today it's probably a succession of mistakes, that he locked the wheel in the pitstop, that we lost a couple of tenths during the pitstop, and then he probably was trying to be optimum on the pitlane release, and he was a bit too early than the optimum.

“I think when you start to do a mistake, it's quite easy to do more than one, and this weekend is a good example of that.

“When we were trying to push during the pitstop, we are losing something. At the pit exit, we were two tenths of a second behind someone, and it's a succession of fact.

“The pace was decent, but we were completely unable to overtake Max at the beginning, then Piastri, and... point taken for the rest of the season.”

title: Cardinals, Jacoby Brissett strike a new deal

fullText:
The Cardinals and quarterback Jacoby Brissett have resolved their differences.

Via ESPN, the team and Brissett have reached an agreement on a new deal.

Brissett signed a two-year deal in 2025 to serve as Kyler Murray's backup. Brissett was thrust into the starting role during the regular season. He entered 2026 as the default QB1.
