The supporters in Manchester endured a long wait on Sunday as the women's fixture was washed out and the men's game delayed by 30 minutes.

But once action got under way, they were treated to a sensational innings from Buttler.

Super Giants suffered early setbacks as Tim Seifert and captain Aiden Markram fell cheaply but Buttler combined power-hitting with deft touches around the ground to bring up his half-century in 31 balls.

The 35-year-old continued to motor after reaching his 50 and his superb innings finally came to end with three balls remaining and with Tom Moores also adding an unbeaten 39 from 17 deliveries, Super Giants recorded a commanding total.

Phoenix made a shaky start in their reply as Josh Tongue (2-21) struck twice in consecutive balls to remove Will Smeed and Rehan Ahmed.

Opener Joe Clarke then fell to Liam Dawson (3-15), before Laurie Evans followed suit to leave Phoenix reeling at 43-4.

title: Gymnast Ward goes from Glasgow dreamer to gold medallist
description: Twelve years ago, a young Reuben Ward watched wide-eyed as Dan Keatings won gymnastics gold for Scotland in Glasgow. Now he celebrates achieving the same feat in the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
Twelve years ago, wee Reuben Ward watched wide-eyed as Dan Keatings won gymnastics gold for Scotland in Glasgow.

That was the day he began dreaming.

In his nine-year-old mind, the notion of competing in the Commonwealth Games for Scotland began to form. Not winning gold. Not even being on a podium. Just pulling on the vest and getting out there.

So when the 21-year-old took the acclaim of an ecstatic Emirates Arena crowd after being announced as the Glasgow 2026 all-around champion, it was all he had ever dreamed of and so much more.

Ward - whose parents Brendan and Lisa left East Kilbride for Bury before he was born - had just become the country's third gold medallist on day three of the Games.

"I remember seeing him win and seeing how it was a big deal to people and I thought 'I want to do that'," Ward told BBC Sport Scotland, recalling Keating's success while in the afterglow of his own.

"So to be here now, having done it myself, is spectacular. It's such a full-circle moment. Glasgow and East Kilbride have been like second homes to me my entire life so to do it here is incredibly special."

Scott overcomes pressure and big pal Dean to give Scotland golden start

Why is it so special to be part of Team Scotland?

All the latest news from Scotland at the Games

There was a sense beforehand that Ward could contend here. A bronze maybe. Perhaps even a silver depending how things go.

His team-mates privately made noises that, should everything fall in his favour, gold could be within reach. They had seen him in training, and performed alongside him in the team event on Friday, where Scotland finished fourth.

They knew he was in a good place.

Ward sat seventh after the floor exercise, but streaked into the lead after a splendid performance on the pommel - routinely his strongest event.

He retained that advantage after the rings - by which point assorted Team Scotland officials and members of the Scottish media had arrived in dribs and drabs, with the sniff of a gold in the air.

Ward's vault had been compromised in the team event by a slight issue in his run up - he had to adapt it on the fly and could only execute two twists - but he nailed it this time, performing three to go into the final two rotations top of the standings.

A strong showing in the parallel bars - and a judicious Team Scotland appeal to add an extra 0.100 - maintained his lead at 0.550, meaning he needed to keep his shape in the horizontal bar to clinch gold.

As he stuck his landing, his coach Jake Seager fell to his knees celebrating before the two embraced. It wasn't official yet, but they knew.

"I like to imagine the best scenario possible and that was winning," added Ward when asked what he was thinking as his head hit the pillow on Saturday night.

"It kept me awake a little bit because I was picturing it and feeling the emotions. But this beat the expectations by a mile.

"Falling short on Friday was heartbreaking and I'm just so overwhelmed, man. I can barely put words together."

It could get even better. He goes on the floor and pommel on Monday, and is a real medal contender in the later.

His celebrations will have to wait for now, but by Tuesday, Ward could well be getting up to all sorts of capers in Glasgow with his Scotland team-mates.

"Tonight looks like eating hotel food and probably getting a pretty bad night's sleep," he said. "Then I'll come in tomorrow, and try to relax and hit my routine.

"On Tuesday, after the competition, I'll celebrate big time with the team, with my boys. I love them so much and them coming to see me at the end when I was going around of the arena was special.

"I'm hoping we'll get to experience a bit of Glasgow.. "

title: Leeds beat Bradford but leaders hit by Sivo injury
description: Leeds Rhinos go two points clear at the top of the Super League standings following a comfortable victory over Bradford Bulls, but suffer a blow with 29-try winger Maika Sivo suffering a suspected broken arm.
fullText:
Tries: McDonnell 2, O'Connor, Holroyd, Croft, Jenkins, Watkins Goals: Connor 7

Tries: Armitage, Ryan Goals: Hooley 2

Leeds Rhinos moved two points clear at the top of Super League following a comfortable victory over Yorkshire rivals Bradford Bulls at Headingley.

James McDonnell scored twice on his 100th Super League appearance for the Rhinos, who bounced back impressively after their surprise defeat to Castleford Tigers last Sunday.

But the Rhinos, who scored seven tries in total, were dealt a blow in the first half when the league's top try scorer Maika Sivo was taken off with a suspected broken forearm arm, which head coach Brad Arthur said could put him on the sidelines for six to eight weeks.

Struggling Bradford, who took the lead through Guy Armitage's try, slipped to a sixth defeat in seven Super League matches.

Leeds winger Sivo suffers suspected broken forearm

Leigh keep rolling with win over rivals Warrington

Giants end 12-match losing run with win at York

The Bulls broke the deadlock in the ninth minute when left edge centre Armitage superbly reached Chris Atkin's deft grubber kick and touched down just within the field of play.

Leeds were then dealt with a major setback as their 29-try wing Sivo picked up an injury when making a tackle on the halfway line and was seen with his right arm in a sling at the end of the game.

The hosts did not let that moment affect them, however, and McDonnell was alert to intercept a pass from Atkin to race clear inside his own half to dive over.

Three minutes after Jake Connor had a try chalked off for a double movement, the Leeds stand-off was in the thick of the action once more, firing a pass out to Kallum Watkins as McDonnell dotted down a simple second try on the right wing.

Rhinos half-back Brodie Croft then weaved in field and presented Jarrod O'Connor with the opportunity to dart through a gap and dive over just to the left of the sticks. Connor slotted the conversion to give the hosts a 12-point lead at the break.

The Bulls were briefly back in the contest within five minutes of the restart when Ethan Ryan caught Riley Dean's up-and-under, found Atkin and then received the return pass to dive over for a superb score on his 200th career appearance.

That proved to be only short respite for the Bulls as moments later Tom Holroyd took advantage of Connor's superb 40-20 kick to barge over from close range to help re-establish Leeds' 12-point advantage.

The Bulls were caught out in the back field when Connor's high kick was not collected by Connor Wynne and Croft pounced to dive over for Leeds' fifth try of the match.

Leeds scored once more on the hour mark when Cooper Jenkins broke through Eliot Peposhi's attempted tackle to dive over on the attacking right edge.

Bradford's day was summed up when Armitage intercepted a pass from Lachie Miller but Ryan knocked on at the vital moment when he threatened to race to the Leeds line.

More magic from Connor then saw Watkins stroll in for another try and Connor slotted the extras to make it seven from seven with the boot.

Leeds Rhinos coach Brad Arthur told BBC Radio Leeds after full-time:

"I was really happy with how courageous we were. I thought we were pretty resilient.

"We could probably play with a little bit more control at times. I felt like we left a few points out there but at least we were able to defend this week."

Bradford Bulls coach Kurt Haggerty told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I feel like we gifted Leeds a lot of what they got in the game. Ultimately, if you keep turning the ball over you're going to get hurt at this level, especially against a very good team.

"I think it was individual errors. It's just those little moments of concentration that get us at the moment.

"I have to look at it and think, 'what do we need?' Can we stay away from going into the loan market, which I'm really proud that we have done so far as a club."

title: Federal officials investigate after a video appears to show a person kicking a California sea lion
description: Federal wildlife authorities are investigating after a video appeared to show a person kicking a protected sea lion at a beach in California.  A spokesperson for the federal National Oceanic and Atmos...
fullText:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Federal wildlife authorities are investigating after a video appeared to show a person kicking a protected sea lion at a beach in California.

A spokesperson for the federal National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration confirmed an ongoing investigation into the incident but declined to provide additional details Sunday.

The video appears to show a person throwing kicks at the sea lion at La Jolla Cove in San Diego as at least one other person can be heard laughing in the background. The person follows the sea lion, throwing more kicks at the animal as it tries to scoot away before the video ends.

"NOAA Fisheries' Office of Law Enforcement is investigating reports of a video on social media that shows an interaction between an individual and sea lion, allegedly in La Jolla Cove," a spokesperson for the agency said. "In the video, the individual appears to be kicking the sea lion. This is an ongoing investigation, and we cannot provide further details at this time."

The person in the video has not been publicly identified.

Sea lions are federally protected under the Marine Mammal Protection Act. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's guidelines say that people should stay at least 50 feet (15 meters) away from sea lions, seals and other species protected by the act.

"This disgusting act of animal cruelty is unacceptable," San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said in a post on X. He acknowledged the federal investigation and said he has directed local law enforcement to review the footage.

title: Romania scrambles F-16 jets and downs a suspected Russian drone, the third in 3 days
description: Romania shot down a suspected Russian drone after it crossed into its airspace on Sunday — the third such incursion in three days in the Eastern European nation that's both a European Union and a NATO...
fullText:
BUCHAREST, Romania (AP) — Romania shot down a suspected Russian drone after it crossed into its airspace on Sunday — the third such incursion in three days in the Eastern European nation that's both a European Union and a NATO member, the country's president said.

Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets scrambled from the Fetești airbase, under NATO's operational command, and shot down the drone over the Black Sea, the military alliance said.

"A new drone was shot down this morning, at 10:13, by an F-16 aircraft of the Romanian Air Force, over the territorial waters of Romania, in the Sulina–Chilia area," Romanian President Nicusor Dan said.

He added that authorities found that one of the earlier intercepted drones appears to be "a Shahed type, used by the Russian Federation in the war of aggression against Ukraine."

This is the fourth recent downing by Romania of a drone violating NATO airspace in coordination with the alliance, said Col. Martin O'Donnell, a spokesperson for NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, known as SHAPE.

Before the last three interceptions, Romanian jets shot down a drone in the sky above Estonia in May, he said. Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania from where they have broad strike capabilities as part of NATO's force posture.

"As we continue to prove, NATO is constantly on the watch and prepared to defend itself from any threat," O'Donnell said.

Romania has acquired the MEROPS counter-drone system, which fires relatively cheap, three-feet long drones to take down incoming Shahed and other variants. That system is part of a broader hardening across the military alliance of NATO's long eastern border against drone threats.

In May, a Russian drone that was part of an attack on Ukraine went astray and struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, injuring two people and raising fears the war could spill over into the alliance's territory.

"It is inadmissible and intolerable that the Russian Federation continues to violate Romanian airspace, which is also NATO and European Union airspace," President Dan said. "Such actions are unacceptable and we treat them with all seriousness, together with our allies."

NATO and EU ally Belgium said Sunday's incursion was a "stark reminder of the ongoing threat Russia's war poses to European security."

"Belgium stands firmly with Romania after several drones were shot down over its territory in the past days. Romania's investigation has already confirmed that one of them was a Russian Shahed drone," the country's Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said, adding that 300 Belgium troops are based in Romania as part of NATO's eastern flank force.

A series of drone incursions by Russia and Ukraine have hit Romania and other NATO members since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

title: Cheaper, open and intelligent: Chinese AI models gain ground, as they make inroads in the US
description: China has a hot new product in the United States: artificial intelligence.  San Francisco-based Raffi Krikorian, the chief technology officer at Mozilla, which runs the Firefox browser, switched to Chinese AI startup Moonshot’s Kimi K3 for many of his day-to-day activities within days of the new, powerful model’s launch more than a week ago.  “It just seems snappier,” he said of K3, comparing it to the acclaimed and more expensive Claude Fable chatbot from San Francisco company Anthropic.
fullText:
HONG KONG (AP) — China has a hot new product in the United States: artificial intelligence.

San Francisco-based Raffi Krikorian, the chief technology officer at Mozilla, which runs the Firefox browser, switched to Chinese AI startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 for many of his day-to-day activities within days of the new, powerful model's launch more than a week ago.

What makes Chinese AI models attractive to American users?

What are Chinese AI companies' business prospects?

How are Chinese AI models competing with US counterparts?

How might US policies impact Chinese AI adoption?

"It just seems snappier," he said of K3, comparing it to the acclaimed and more expensive Claude Fable chatbot from San Francisco company Anthropic. Earlier, he had been using another high-performing Chinese model, Z.ai's GLM-5.2, for routine tasks such as managing his calendar, documents and email.

Krikorian is one of a growing number of Americans adopting Chinese AI systems, which are gaining ground around the world because they are more affordable and increasingly efficient. U.S. companies like cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase said they're switching to Chinese AI models to help trim costs.

Their popularity has frustrated some U.S. tech giants, but short of an outright ban, they're likely to continue to appeal to independent software developers in the U.S. and elsewhere.

American-led restrictions block China from accessing some of the world's most advanced technologies including cutting-edge AI chips and U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned more sanctions could be coming to protect American intellectual property.

U.S. President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday accused Moonshot of using "covert" but not necessarily illegal methods to build K3 off the back of Anthropic's Fable. Some U.S. politicians and AI companies including Anthropic have accused Chinese startups of illicit "distillation" of their models to extract their technologies, a claim that Beijing rejects as "groundless."

The rapid rise of cutting-edge Chinese AI models this year shows the China-U.S. race in AI has moved on from early last year, when Chinese startup DeepSeek shook up the U.S. technology industry and put China on the map with an AI model that performed on par with those in the U.S. but much more cheaply.

The latest AI models launched by startups Z.ai, or Zhipu, in June, and Moonshot in July are nearly as intelligent as the frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, experts say. Also in July, China's Alibaba previewed its Qwen3.8 Max AI model. In April, DeepSeek rolled out previews of its latest V4 model, challenging OpenAI's GPT and Google's Gemini.

Those constant advances are bearing fruit. Curt Meinhold, a Greensboro, North Carolina-based technology executive, said he increasingly prefers to use DeepSeek for tasks such as finding business leads or ways to generate sales.

title: Cajun Navy leader warns Nolan Wells' search area has deadly 'washing machine' currents: 'Lots of drownings'
description: A United Cajun Navy leader says the waters near Horn Island where Nolan Wells was found are known as a "washing machine" due to deadly rip currents.
fullText:
MISSISSIPPI – A United Cajun Navy leader who helped search for Nolan Wells says the water around where the teen was found is notorious for deadly "washing machine" currents, and water conditions the day he vanished were far from ideal.

Wells, 18, disappeared July 4 after a boat trip with friends to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. A National Park Service ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip two days later, on July 6, after crews searched the area.

Wells' friends returned to the mainland that afternoon without him. Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter has said investigators believe Wells chose to stay on the island. It wasn't until later that night that his mother learned from one of Wells' friends that he was missing, and she reported it to authorities.

Search Called Off After Body Matching Missing Teen Nolan Wells Found Off Mississippi Coast

The stretch of water between Horn Island, where Wells was found dead, and neighboring Ship Island is known to locals as a "washing machine" because of its deadly rip currents, United Cajun Navy Vice President Brian Trascher told Fox News Digital. Authorities previously told the Associated Press that foul play isn't suspected.

"Yeah, there is some kind of nickname for it, and it's because they've had a lot of drownings in that area and on that island. And to the west, there's Ship Island, just another few miles to the West. And in between those two islands, there's a strong divergent occurrence," Trascher said. "And that area is called the washing machine by locals."

Based on conversations with people who were on Horn Island on July 4, Trascher said the rip current that day was "extremely strong," adding that the water off the island's northwest tip can go from shallow to deep in just a few steps.

Nolan Wells' Hometown Officials Rally Behind Sheriff After 'Derelict In Their Duties' Attack

While Wells knew how to swim and swam regularly, Trascher said a strong rip current can overpower even an experienced swimmer, especially if panic, sun exposure or alcohol are factors.

Like What You're Reading? Click Here For More

Trascher said one of the biggest unresolved questions in Wells' death is what happened between when he was last seen, around 4 or 4:30 p.m. on July 4, and when his body was found, calling it a "gaping hole" that still needs to be answered.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"I've heard virtually no explanation, no eyewitness accounts. Nobody seemed to see him after that... there don't seem to be any photographs or videos of him after that time. So what happened? It wasn't dark yet. There was still a lot of people on the island... why did he just vanish and show up dead two days later?" Trascher said. "That is a question that needs to be asked. And I'm not suggesting that means that there was foul play involved. I'm just saying that there is a gaping hole in the story that needs to filled."

Nolan Wells Independent Autopsy Doesn't Point To Foul Play, Former Medical Examiner Says

During a Wednesday news conference, attorney Ben Crump revealed that an area of "red discoloration" was found on Wells' head, but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed an independent autopsy, couldn't come to a conclusion on a cause or manner of death "pending further investigation." An official autopsy into Wells' death hasn't been completed.

When asked by Fox News Digital about the case, forensic pathologist Dr. Michael Baden said the head injury doesn't point to foul play.

"So that could be from bumping into something in the water. There's a lot of debris in the water, for example. It depends how deep it is, but it's describing a really superficial impact that could have happened before death or after death," Baden said. "What he's describing is a minor injury that could be... totally innocent."

Without having additional information, Mitchell wrote in his report that he couldn't rule out the possibility that "non-accidental factors contributed to or caused the death."

title: Gittens keen to impress 'world-class' Alonso
description: Chelsea winger Jamie Gittens says he will be involved in Xabi Alonso's squad next season and describes his new manager as "one of the best to do it".
fullText:
Chelsea winger Jamie Gittens says he will be involved in Xabi Alonso's squad next season and describes his new manager as "one of the best to do it".

The 21-year-old joined the Blues from Borussia Dortmund in a £52m deal last summer but struggled to make a major impact in his first season at Stamford Bridge.

Asked whether he had been told he was part of Alonso's plans, Gittens initially replied: "Yeah."

He continued: "He just wants me to keep being positive, to keep taking on players, to keep creating chances and to keep pushing myself to the maximum."

Gittens added that the squad respect Alonso because he was a "world-class midfielder" during his playing career with Real Madrid and Liverpool, among others.

He also said that when he faced Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen side while playing in Germany, it was "really hard". Leverkusen won the Bundesliga title and German Cup in Alonso's first full season in charge.

Gittens added: "They were really a team."

Team cohesion was something Chelsea lacked last season as they finished 10th in the Premier League, failed to qualify for European football and ended the campaign without a trophy.

However, he is confident that signings like £117m British transfer record Morgan Rogers, who he played with in Manchester City's academy, "will raise the bar" and that Chelsea retain an ambition to "win everything".

Gittens is also back on track having scored in Alonso's first two matches behind closed doors against EFL clubs Crawley and Bromley, having suffered a hamstring injury in January and missing the back end of last season.

He insists he is "90% fit" after a holiday training camp in Portugal and Spain.

However, he admitted: "It has been hard because this was the first muscle injury I've had. I'm feeling much better, the hamstrings are good.

"I want to succeed here. I need to show people what I can do. I've shown small glimpses, I would say, but this season will be a good season."

title: Mayo beat Kerry in thriller to end 75-year All-Ireland wait
description: Mayo end a 75-year wait for the county's fourth All-Ireland Senior Football title with a 1-20 to 1-17 victory over Kerry in a captivating and intense final that went down to the wire at a raucous Croke Park.
fullText:
Mayo ended a 75-year wait for the county's fourth All-Ireland Senior Football title with a 1-20 to 1-17 victory over Kerry in a captivating and intense final that went down to the wire at a raucous Croke Park.

In remarkable scenes, the emotion came pouring out of the Mayo squad and supporters as they lifted three quarters of a century worth of pain with a ferocious and tireless performance that denied Kerry a second straight title.

Mayo, who came into the game having lost 13 finals - including two replays - since their 1951 triumph, suffered a slow start and fell 1-6 to 0-3 behind in the opening exchanges as talisman David Clifford's goal helped Kerry establish early dominance.

But Mayo bounced back and trailed by only a point at 1-8 to 0-10 at half-time before surging clear in the third quarter, with Darragh Beirne's goal helping the Westerners build a five-point lead.

Kerry clawed their way back and sat just two points down as they chased a late leveller, but they failed to strike before Tommy Conroy's score capped a famous win for Mayo.

It also provided an unforgettable conclusion to a whirlwind first season under manager Andy Moran - who lost six finals during his Mayo playing days - and sends starlet Kobe McDonald off to Australia an All-Ireland champion at just 18 years of age.

"We kept the faith. We're All-Ireland champions," said an overjoyed Mayo captain Jack Coyne.

"This is what every day of my life I've dreamed of doing. To be able to do this, I can't put it into words."

All-Ireland final: Watch reaction as Mayo lift Sam Maguire after historic win

It would not be a big day at Croke Park for Mayo without pain for their long-suffering fans - and it came early this year during a nervy opening 15 minutes when Kerry threatened to dart off into the distance.

With the always-excellent Paudie Clifford influential early on, Kerry feasted on Mayo nerves to register the game's three opening scores, with David Clifford striking twice after Dylan Casey fisted over the bar.

It could have been worse for Mayo, who breathed a sigh of relief when Sean O'Brien shot wide after receiving a Sean O'Shea fist pass and turning sharply to outfox his marker Bob Tuohy.

While David McBrien delivered a nerve-settling score for Mayo, the high-pressing Westerners kicked a succession of shots short during the opening quarter as they favoured low-percentage efforts in a bid to ramp up scoreboard pressure.

Kerry's scores seemed to come easier, and when a Sean O'Shea effort was followed by Clifford sneaking in behind Donnacha McHugh, rounding Jack Livingstone and blasting the ball into the net, there was a sense that the game was already slipping away from the Connacht county.

But back they came. Armed with ferocious intent and a forward line ravenous for turnover ball, Mayo rattled Kerry during a period when they clawed back from seven points down to revive their hopes.

Suddenly it was Kerry shots going awry, with David Clifford's two-point free missing after Jack Carney had raised an orange flag at the Hill 16 end.

While Sean O'Shea fisted a score to put Kerry 1-6 to 0-3 up, Ryan O'Donoghue's superb two-pointer, coupled with Tommy Conroy's introduction for Paul Towey, breathed new life into the Mayo cause.

Indeed, after Darragh Beirne and O'Donoghue frees and a Sam Callinan score, Kerry's lead was cut to one at 1-6 to 0-8. After Tom O'Sullivan's score, Beirne and Conroy struck to draw Mayo level, although a cleverly worked point from totemic Kingdom midfielder Joe O'Connor ensured Kerry held a slender advantage at the break.

Lifted by a spirited second-quarter showing, Mayo emerged for the second half and continued to rattle Kerry, shutting down space and flooding forward in numbers.

It paid dividends during a crucial 10-minute period after the restart when a Beirne point and McDonald's '45 put Mayo ahead before Beirne side-footed a cool finish into the Kerry net after O'Donoghue and David McBrien combined in a flowing attack.

"I had envisioned during the week that the ball would get flicked across to me and I was going to hit it top right," said Beirne of his goal.

"When the ball came to me, I just put the foot through it, saw it nestle in the top corner and the rest is history."

Substitute Keith Evans replied for a rocked Kerry, but Jack Carney's nailed two-pointed effort put Mayo 1-14 to 1-9 ahead and amid a barely conceivable cacophony of noise from the Croke Park stands.

Wary of not panicking, Kerry reeled off the next four scores to pull within one but their hopes were kept alive by goalkeeper Shane Murphy, who tipped Kobe McDonald's goal-bound shot over the bar.

After David Clifford fisted over the bar, Mayo again streaked clear when the brilliant O'Donoghue landed a two-pointer after another McDonald score to put Moran's men 1-19 to 1-14 in front.

In a frantic and incredibly tense closing 10 minutes, brothers David and Paudie Clifford combined for three points to bring Kerry back to within two.

Chasing a late shooting opportunity, Kerry held on to the ball before Sean O'Shea's do-or-die effort from outside the two-point arc dropped short.

Having regained possession, Mayo - as they had done so often - streamed forward and found Conroy, who kicked the insurance score to ensure Mayo's success and spark ecstatic scenes among the green and red fans at Croke Park.

title: Norris wins his first grand prix of year in Hungary
description: Lando Norris takes his and McLaren's first victory of the year in a compelling Hungarian Grand Prix.
fullText:
Lando Norris took his and McLaren's first grand prix victory of the year in a compelling race in Hungary.

As the world champion cruised to a comfortable victory, there was a tense fight for the remaining podium positions in the closing laps between Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli.

Verstappen just managed to hold on while Antonelli took third to extend his championship lead to 50 points over Lewis Hamilton and 59 over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who finished seventh after a bad start.

Ferrari's Hamilton finished the grand prix on Antonelli's tail in fourth place but was penalised five seconds for speeding in the pit lane and dropped to fifth behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri led for most of the first half of the race but retired from second place with a gearbox failure.

Norris said he was "happy to be back and be number one again", adding: "My pace today was probably some of the best pace I've ever had. The car was beautiful to drive and I had confidence."

The key stories of the race were:

Norris' victory, helped by a controversial strategy that did not please his team-mate Piastri

A surprise second for Verstappen after a strategy gamble paid off for Red Bull

Yet another penalty harming Hamilton's prospects in a disappointing race for Ferrari given their pace

A positive weekend for Aston Martin with their new car, despite not scoring points

Norris' concern before the start would have been about the losing a place to Leclerc, who was starting second behind the Briton.

The McLaren driver made a good start, the challenge from Leclerc never materialised, but instead Norris lost the lead to Piastri.

Norris was leading through Turn Two, but a strong start put the Australian second, and when Norris made an error and ran wide through Turn Two, Piastri seized his opportunity to take the lead.

That left McLaren with a quandary for although their cars were running one-two, the slower one was in the lead, and they were concerned about threats from behind.

Piastri led through the first pit stops, with Norris never much more than a second behind, but Norris started to challenge hard in the second stint and wanted to be given the opportunity to challenge his team-mate.

Norris asked to make his second stop first but was refused.

Instead, Piastri was called in, McLaren saying they were covering the threat from Hamilton, who had just stopped himself, and Norris was allowed to run for six further laps before making his pit call for fresh tyres, using his pace to gain time.

As Norris made his stop, Piastri was delayed by a collision with Williams driver Carlos Sainz while lapping the Spaniard, who was penalised five seconds for the incident.

Piastri was clearly unhappy, telling his engineer not to talk to him shortly after Norris returned to the track just ahead of his team-mate.

Piastri said afterwards that his anger was directed at Sainz, and that he believed he would still have been ahead of Norris had it not been for the collision. He had no complaints about strategy.

Piastri had just been promoted back to second place by Antonelli's second pit stop when he lost use of his gearbox on lap 56 and pulled off after Turn Three.

That led to a late virtual safety car (VSC) which enlivened the battles behind Norris, but he was untouchable as he and McLaren, who came to Hungary with an upgraded car, revived memories of some of their dominant victories of their championship last year.

Verstappen was unhappy with his car for much of the race, with regular complaints on team radio, but Red Bull pulled a masterstroke when they fitted soft tyres to his car at his second pit stop.

The aim was to challenge Hamilton in the later laps after the seven-time champion made an early second stop with 40 laps still to go.

It was heading towards a tense climax when Piastri's retirement brought out the VSC.

That prompted a late round of pit stops, Ferrari bringing in both their drivers and putting them behind Verstappen.

Hamilton came out of the pits and passed Antonelli into the first corner, after the Italian stayed out under the VSC, but had to give the place back after the restart because the Mercedes driver had just passed the key line on the track in front.

Antonelli and Hamilton started chasing back towards Verstappen, but they were delayed while lapping Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.

That looked as if it might be decisive, but in the end Verstappen was comfortably able to keep Antonelli at bay, crossing the line 3.6 seconds ahead.

Another key point in Verstappen's race had been his re-passing of Hamilton after the Ferrari had got briefly ahead following the first pit stops.

That gave him clear air and enabled the Dutchman to consolidate his race position in third place behind the McLarens, laying the foundations for Red Bull's late strategy call.

Hamilton will leave Hungary ruing another penalty - the one for speeding in the pit lane was his second in two days after behind penalised for blocking Piastri in qualifying, and follows two others at the previous two races in Belgium and Britain.

Behind him, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, ahead of Russell, who dropped to 21st place on the first lap after his anti-stall kicked in at the start, and fought back strongly.

At Aston Martin, Lance Stroll finished in 13th, ahead of team-mate Fernando Alonso, their positions dictated to a degree by luck under the VSC and their divergent strategies.

But the key point was that Alonso, in particular, was able to fight with other cars for the first time, and he ran a long first stint on the soft tyres, before switching to the mediums, which was a bold strategy.

The long-awaited upgrade to their car, which was new apart from the front suspension, engine and gearbox, has reduced their lap times by about two seconds.

A Honda engine upgrade is due for the Dutch Grand Prix, the next race in four weeks' time after the summer break, which the team hope will elevate them further and potentially bring the possibility of the occasional points finish into the picture.

title: Chiesa happy but wants new chapter at Liverpool
description: Liverpool forward Federico Chiesa says he is "happy" at the club amid speculation over his future.
fullText:
Federico Chiesa insists he is only "thinking about Liverpool" amid continued speculation over his future.

Across two seasons at Anfield under Arne Slot, the Italian forward has started one Premier League game and scored just five times in 50 appearances across all competitions.

The 28-year-old, who joined from Juventus in a deal worth £12.5m in 2024 and is contracted until 2028, told La Gazzetta dello Sport, external in June: "If I don't find consistency in the Premier League, I'll have to look elsewhere."

But after scoring in the first friendly of the Andoni Iraola era on Saturday where Liverpool beat Sunderland 4-2, Chiesa told reporters: "Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool. I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything.

"I am doing the best I can to have a chance here - and then we will see.

"At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool."

Asked whether it was a fresh start under new boss Iraola - appointed in June after Slot's dismissal - Chiesa added: "I don't know - it is difficult to say. It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year.

"Maybe there have been too many fresh starts. But I don't care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager. Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best too.

"Last year, I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is.

"The gaffer decided to do so, he had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that."

title: Complete weekend for Norris but poor result for Sainz - driver ratings
description: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Hungarian Grand Prix.
fullText:
World champion Lando Norris took victory from pole position in Hungary on Sunday to secure his and McLaren's first grand prix win of 2026.

Norris was passed for the lead by team-mate Oscar Piastri at the start but the Australian later retired from the race with a gearbox failure.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second and title leader Kimi Antonelli claimed the final podium in place in third.

Lewis Hamilton, who was given a three-place grid penalty before the race for impeding Piastri in qualifying, dropped from fourth to fifth at the chequered flag, after he was handed a five-second time penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Hungary.

The complete weekend McLaren and Norris have been waiting for. Pole position, outstanding pace when finally released into clear air and a controlled run to the flag earned him his first grand prix victory of the season, even if losing the lead on lap one was a minor blemish.

Dragged a difficult Red Bull to a result that looked unlikely after qualifying. He battled constant issues with his car throughout the weekend but still put himself in the right position to inherit second when Piastri retired.

A strong damage-limitation drive from Mercedes' championship leader. His failure to slow sufficiently for yellow flags in qualifying compromised his starting position, but recovering from seventh to the podium and holding off the Ferraris was an impressive response.

Ferrari looked extremely quick on Friday but Leclerc was unable to turn that promise into a podium. Lost positions to Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the start and finished fifth on the road before Hamilton's penalty promoted him.

The fastest Ferrari driver across the weekend, but two costly penalties undid much of the good work. He missed pole by just 0.012 seconds and raced strongly, yet impeding Piastri in qualifying and speeding in the pit lane turned a potential podium into fifth.

A quieter weekend from Hadjar. Qualified and finished comfortably inside the points and brought home sixth on a day when his more experienced team-mate demonstrated how difficult the Red Bull was to drive.

An excellent recovery after anti-stall dropped him from sixth to 21st at the start. Qualifying was disrupted by a water leak and his race appeared ruined within seconds, but the Mercedes driver fought his way back to seventh to rescue valuable points.

Admitted he underperformed in qualifying but put that right with a very good race. Used his fresher tyres to pass team-mate Arvid Lindblad late on and led Racing Bulls home in eighth.

A deserved points finish after reaching Q3 and keeping himself at the front of the midfield battle. Passed Lindblad late on and comfortably outperformed Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto across the weekend.

Another strong rookie weekend. Reached Q3 despite missing most of final practice and made an ambitious one-stop strategy work well enough to claim the final point, although Lawson got the better of him.

Norris wins his first grand prix of year in Hungary

Recovered well from a disappointing qualifying session and came close to making his one-stop strategy pay off. Finishing just outside the points was respectable, but Hulkenberg held a clear advantage within the Audi team.

A steady weekend in an Alpine that never looked capable of challenging the leading midfield runners. Qualified and finished ahead of team-mate Franco Colapinto but there was little opportunity to achieve much more.

Lost valuable practice time following a suspension failure and started near the back, so recovering to 13th was more than a solid result. Aston Martin's upgrade provided encouragement and Stroll made reasonable use of it on Sunday.

Reaching Q2 for the first time this season represented genuine progress for Aston Martin. Finished behind team-mate Stroll after starting four places ahead, but this was still the most competitive weekend the team has produced in 2026.

His crash in second practice immediately put Alpine on the back foot. Qualified a respectable 13th but slipped behind team-mate Gasly and both Aston Martins during an underwhelming race.

Out-qualified team-mate Oliver Bearman for the first time since Monaco and led Haas home. The car lacked the pace to contend for points, but Ocon at least extracted more from the difficult weekend than Bearman.

Williams expected the Hungaroring to expose the cars' weaknesses and that proved to be the case. Albon qualified behind Carlos Sainz but led his team-mate home in a race where neither car looked remotely competitive.

A difficult weekend in an unpredictable Williams ended with a penalty for his collision with Piastri while being lapped. The car's limitations were obvious, but the incident added another unnecessary complication to a poor result.

Out-qualified and outraced by team-mate Ocon during a painful weekend for Haas. A five-second penalty for ignoring blue flags compounded an afternoon spent near the back of the field.

A result that does not reflect the quality of his drive. Produced a superb move to take the lead at Turn Two and was ahead in the first half of the race. Didn't look like he could match McLaren team-mate Norris for pure pace, though, and once Norris jumped him in the pits, looked resigned to finishing behind him. A suspected gearbox failure robbed him of well-deserved points.

Qualified last, started from the pit lane following set-up changes and retired with a problem at the front-left of the Cadillac. There was very little positive performance to assess.

Started ahead of Perez but Cadillac's struggles meant his race was similarly shortlived. Overheating brakes forced his retirement before he had any meaningful chance to make progress.

title: Inside the growing vigilante movement to knock out Flock surveillance cameras
description:
An underground network of privacy activists is disabling or destroying the ubiquitous surveillance devices sprouting up across the US
The first time that “NoMark” tried to knock out a Flock camera feed, he waited an hour for the perfect moment – pacing in and out of bushes that towered over him, a few feet behind a pole holding up the device.
“I was just so nervous,” he said.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
The first time that “NoMark” tried to knock out a Flock camera feed, he waited an hour for the perfect moment – pacing in and out of bushes that towered over him, a few feet behind a pole holding up the device.

“I was just so nervous,” he said.

NoMark, as he’s known on Instagram, had already gained an online following of hundreds of thousands for posting videos of himself wearing a black mask and taking on small-time vigilante missions: breaking up fights outside a bar and breaking into a refinery he believed was “polluting the city real bad”. The Minnesota Star Tribune dubbed him “Minneapolis’ Batman”. He spoke to the Guardian under condition of anonymity to discuss potentially illegal acts.

On this June night, he set his sights on a new target: automated license plate readers (ALPRs) made by the US company Flock Safety.

This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.

These black cameras, which are hooked up to a rectangular solar panel and typically mounted on a pole, snap photos of passing vehicles and run the pictures against large databases. They have sparked nationwide backlash from pro-privacy critics, who point to public records suggesting that these devices can help law enforcement keep tabs on specific license plates and the people driving these cars. That they can sweep in so many people’s location from an innocent act in a public space – regardless of whether the target is a suspect in a crime, and without a warrant – has led to fears of mass surveillance.

Flock, based in Georgia and valued at $8.4bn, says its cameras scan license plates billions of times each month in about 6,000 communities in nearly every state in the US.

The company said in a February blogpost that its ALPRs are “not mass surveillance tools” and that it “cannot track vehicles, much less individual people”.

Across the street from a Taco Bell, NoMark couldn’t stop thinking about whether he would get caught, and the adrenaline felt paralyzing – even though this felt “on brand” for his online persona, which has won him more than 700,000 followers on Instagram and TikTok. After a few minutes of not spotting any cars on the road, he climbed a few feet up the pole, taped up the camera to block its lens and snipped the wires that powered the whole operation. Then he ended his phone’s recording and fled.

Nowadays, NoMark is much calmer on these excursions, and it only takes him a few minutes to get the job done after having taken down more than a dozen cameras, he says. But he still assumes the police are looking for him. Even if he does get arrested, he’s hopeful the charges won’t be too severe – and more important, he “just wants to send a message”.

“I’m not afraid to do things if I think they’re right,” he says. “These things are coming up so fast across the country that this is kind of the only way to combat them.”

The Minneapolis camera destroyer is not alone. As anger grows towards law enforcement contracts with Flock, vigilantes across the country are taking matters into their own hands by smashing, obstructing or taking down these cameras. Many are leaning into their creative side: “paint bombing” the devices, planting American flags at the scene after damaging them, 3D printing objects to help obstruct the camera’s view and leaving colorful messages like “hahaha get wrecked ya surveilling fucks”. Some influencers are even creating fake cease-and-desist letters from Flock, capitalizing on the company’s negative public perception.

The Guardian has identified at least 33 instances of people damaging, vandalizing and destroying Flock cameras, across 23 states, that appear to have the explicit message of protesting surveillance.

This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.

Flock, along with police departments across the US, say these cameras are integral for public safety, and capture vehicle details that can help in investigations, such as license plate numbers and the make and model of vehicles. Flock’s website also advertises how these cameras can “stop crime in real time” by alerting officers “the moment a suspect car passes by” – suggesting that cops can act quickly on these leads to pursue a target. The company’s CEO, Garrett Langley, has described some pro-privacy critics as wanting to “normalize lawlessness” and “weaken public safety”.

NoMark has not been caught in his campaign against Flock cameras. Others are facing charges. Jeffrey Sovern in Suffolk, Virginia, has been charged with destruction of property for allegedly damaging more than a dozen Flock cameras. Sovern has not admitted to the act but did tell police that he finds these cameras to be unconstitutional.

He wrote on a GoFundMe created to pay for legal expenses: “I will take the silver lining that this can be a catalyst in a bigger movement to roll back intrusive surveillance.”

A handful of other cases have drawn criminal charges, too. In New Mexico, Jevon Martinez was arrested after allegedly destroying 13 Flock cameras.

When asked if he would “continue to take down these Flock cameras”, Martinez told local news station KRQE: “Absolutely. They are a clear and present threat to public safety.” The news outlet also reported that a sign near one of the damaged Flock cameras read: “You’re welcome, the Republic of New Mexico.”

Flock did not comment on vigilantes knocking out its cameras but did publish a blogpost in mid-July about helping government agencies respond if a camera is damaged.

“We’ve planned for it,” the company wrote, adding that protection plans are available for purchase.

Law enforcement is aware of the backlash and responding. Dozens of state fusion centers – collaborative hubs where federal and local agencies share intelligence about crime and terrorism – circulated memos across law enforcement agencies this summer directing officers to monitor anti-Flock advocacy as part of a directive to protect national security, according to reporting from journalist Dan Boguslaw. One report Boguslaw obtained from a Wisconsin intelligence agency calls for increased vigilance and patrols during protests and events such as a “national week of action” in mid-August. That intelligence digest also advised local law enforcement to report “vandalism, disruption or sabotage” of ALPRs to fusion centers.

The winds of sympathy online are not blowing in Flock’s favor. News articles and videos about vigilantes’ cases have drawn support from online commenters, who post made-up, neighborly alibis like seeing accused parties rescuing dogs or serving meals at a soup kitchen at the time a camera was destroyed.

The anti-Flock online ecosystem also features an exchange of tips and strategies for kneecapping the cameras. One Reddit poster shared a 3D print file for an object he says can help block cameras without damaging them or violating vandalism laws.

NoMark, in Minneapolis, says he receives dozens of messages daily from people wanting to help, letting him know they’re taking similar actions or asking for advice on staying safe. He keeps his replies vague, as he doesn’t want his words to get people arrested. He tells those writing to him to avoid driving past the cameras, and to make sure they’re going out late at night when they no one else is around. He reiterates that they should cover up completely, including their face and hands.

He also tells them: “Always cover the camera.”

Minneapolis’s Batman thinks you need both political pressure on elected officials and vigilantism to achieve change. He believes showing up to city council meetings – and he’s shown up to a few without his mask – is helpful but “it does obviously take time, and it’s not always effective”.

“The more time you take, the more data they get on people,” he said.

More than 80 cities have disbanded, decided not to renew or rejected contracts with Flock in recent years, or deactivated the company’s cameras, including Austin and Denver, although activists remain concerned about the devices’ continued use in those areas.

Beyond general surveillance creep, privacy advocates fear US Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s ability to access these camera feeds through legal loopholes to pursue immigrants.

Police officers have used the cameras for their own personal ends as well. Several have lost their jobs after misusing the devices to stalk people. Though license plate reading is the cameras’ bread and butter, 404 Media reported last week that cops have used Flock’s search feature to look for people with distinct markers – like tattoos and specific T-shirts – and not just cars.

Congress is taking note, and earlier this month a Texas lawmaker introduced a bill requiring warrants for data collected by Flock cameras.

Not all anti-Flock activism takes the form of camera destruction. A crowdsourced map created by the grassroots group DeFlock maps out more than 115,000 ALPRs across the country. The organization’s site also allows users to see if their license plates have been searched in Flock’s system, get directions to avoid ALPRs and find upcoming meetings about municipal Flock contracts.

Flock’s CEO has taken note of DeFlock’s advocacy, too, and characterized the organization as “terroristic” but recently apologized for that label. In a tweet, he attributed DeFlock’s popularity to his company’s “inadequate response to the questions and concerns that people have about ALPR”. The company is adapting to the backlash, canceling an always-on recording feature, “human distress detection”, which was intended to detect screaming.

A local chapter of DeFlock, in Norfolk, Virginia, says it does not endorse vigilantes targeting Flock cameras but does not advocate against it, either.

The Virginia chapter is working to ensure the city either cancels or does not renew its contract with Flock, but so far it hasn’t had success, and members are particularly angry about speaking restrictions on the topic. At a city council meeting last month, the mayor enforced a rule about reducing repetitive comments to limit the number of speakers who wanted to share their concerns about Flock, the Virginian-Pilot reported.

“We recognize it’s the inevitable outcome of a system designed to prevent people’s voices from being heard,” said a DeFlock spokesperson.

Alex Bowman's Exit Creates NASCAR's Most Coveted Opening
description: Alex Bowman will leave NASCAR on his own terms after 2027, but his decision creates a rare opportunity that could shape Hendrick Motorsports for the next decade.
fullText:
When news broke last week that Alex Bowman would retire from full-time NASCAR Cup Series competition after the 2027 season, it was both unexpected and entirely understandable.

Unexpected because Bowman is only 33 years old. By modern NASCAR standards, that's hardly retirement age. He'll walk away after just 13 full seasons at the sport's highest level, an age when many Cup drivers are still adding to their resumes rather than wrapping them up.

Understandable because Bowman's career has repeatedly been interrupted by injuries that have forced him to confront the physical toll of racing. A concussion sidelined him for five races in 2022. Another crash the following season resulted in a fractured vertebra that cost him three more starts. This year, recurring vertigo symptoms forced him out of four races.

It was easy to assume those setbacks finally convinced Bowman it was time.

It turns out Bowman had been planning this exit long before vertigo entered the conversation.

"It's always been in this time frame," Bowman said Friday. "I would say like kind of this three-year block. Whether it was 2026, '27 or '28, that's something we've talked about for a really long time and what I've always had circled."

That doesn't mean this season didn't test his resolve.

Bowman admitted the vertigo episodes had him considering walking away even sooner.

"I had looked at this year being it quite a bit," Bowman said before adding, "If it was my choice, I wouldn't have made a retirement announcement. I would have just raced until the end of next year and disappeared, but that's not how this sport works."

Unlike many drivers whose careers end because performance fades or organizations decide it's time to move on, Bowman is leaving because he believes the timing is right.

That makes his retirement story unusual.

But what happens next may be even more interesting.

Bowman's departure creates one of the most coveted openings in NASCAR.

The No. 48 Chevrolet at Hendrick Motorsports doesn't become available very often. In fact, seats at NASCAR's most successful organization rarely open at all. When they do, they're the racing equivalent of getting the call from the New York Yankees or Kansas City Chiefs: an opportunity capable of changing a driver's career overnight.

Naturally, speculation has already begun.

Connor Zilisch, Corey Heim and Corey Day have all surfaced as potential candidates. Whether any of them ultimately lands the ride remains to be seen, but Hendrick Motorsports has something most organizations rarely enjoy when a star driver departs: time.

More than a full season's worth of it.

That gives the organization an opportunity to evaluate prospects, monitor development, negotiate contracts and decide what direction it wants its future to take.

The decision may say as much about Hendrick Motorsports as it does the driver who eventually gets the job.

William Byron is just 28 and entering what should be the prime of his career. Chase Elliott is 31. Kyle Larson is 33. None appears close to leaving the sport, yet Bowman becomes the first member of Hendrick's current core to voluntarily step aside.

Will the organization simply look for the best available replacement, or begin preparing for the next generation of Hendrick Motorsports?

So far, the company isn't showing its hand.

"I think we're fortunate enough that we don't go through this all that often at Hendrick Motorsports," president Jeff Andrews said. "And when these cycles do happen, obviously there's a process there of looking for someone with the right fit, not only from a performance standpoint, but for our company and our culture."

For now, though, the focus remains on the driver who is leaving, not the one who will eventually replace him.

"In the near future, it'll be about Alex and his story," Andrews said. "We'll begin that process on what's next for the No. 48 team in 2028 very soon."

So, for the near future it will be all about saying goodbye and Bowman leaving on his own terms.

"This is kind of always what I wanted," he said. "This sport has given me a lot. I love this sport, obviously. I love NASCAR racing. I think the guys that race forever, that's super cool. That just was never going to be me. I'm excited for what the rest of my life holds. I'm honestly really just ready to be a normal person, in a lot of ways."

Alex Bowman still has one more full season to chase victories, make one final playoff run and close out his career.

Hendrick Motorsports has that same amount of time to answer a very different question.

Until a contract is signed, one of the most coveted seats in NASCAR remains open for 2028. Every ambitious driver climbing the sport's ladder knows exactly what that opportunity represents.

For Bowman, the finish line is finally in sight.

For everyone else, the race to replace him has already begun.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: WNBA smashes previous All-Star Game attendance record as Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese feature
description: The 2026 WNBA All-Star Game set a new league attendance record at the United Center in Chicago. Team Spoon walked out of the game with a 129-122 win over Team Coop, named after the two WNBA legends, Cynthia Cooper and Teresa Weatherspoon, who served as general managers.
fullText:
The 2026 WNBA All-Star Game set a new league attendance record at the United Center in Chicago.

Team Spoon walked out of the game with a 129-122 win over Team Coop, named after the two WNBA legends, Cynthia Cooper and Teresa Weatherspoon, who served as general managers.

Team Spoon featured WNBA stars such as Caitlin Clark and A’ja Wilson, while the losing side had the likes of Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese. This star power led to WNBA history being made.

The 2026 WNBA All-Star Game in Chicago Bulls’ United Center brought in 19,783 fans, a big improvement from the 16,988 attendees of the 2025 All-Star Game in Indianapolis.

The previous WNBA All-Star Game attendance record was 19,487, which was set in 2007 at the Verizon Center in Washington, D.C.

Jonquel Jones (22 PTS, 13 REB, 8 AST) was the MVP for Team Spoon off the bench, as stars like Clark (17 PTS, 4 REB, 5 AST) and Wilson (12 PTS) had decent cameos.

Team Coop had two notable performers in Kelsey Mitchell (28 PTS, 4 REB) and Marina Mabrey off the bench (23 PTS).

Angel Reese played just nine minutes in the game, going scoreless but grabbing five rebounds and dishing out four assists.

With the WNBA’s surging popularity in recent years, we’re bound to see more attendance records set in the future in venues that can accommodate 22,000+ fans at a minimum.

The WNBA has broken past the 20,000 viewer barrier multiple times in the past, with the most-attended WNBA game of all time being a two-way tie, both hosting 22,076 fans at the Palace of Auburn Hills in Detroit.

The record was set during the 2003 WNBA Finals between the Detroit Shock and the Los Angeles Sparks, with the 2007 WNBA Finals clash between the Shock and Phoenix Mercury tying that number.

The regular-season record was set earlier this month when the WNBA’s newest franchise, Toronto Tempo, welcomed 20,996 fans in Montreal’s Bell Center for a game against the Dallas Wings.

title: Real Madrid star heading for summer exit as two leading options emerge
description: Real Madrid are closing in on the signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, and that deal will have a knock-on effect for Franco Mastantuono. The 18-year-old has struggled to make his mark during his f...
fullText:
Real Madrid are closing in on the signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, and that deal will have a knock-on effect for Franco Mastantuono. The 18-year-old has struggled to make his mark during his first 12 months in the Spanish capital, and with increased competition on the way, it is very likely that he departs on a temporary basis.

Real Madrid are still counting on Mastantuono, but the feeling is that he will not be in Jose Mourinho’s plans for the 2026-27 season. As such, Diario AS have reported that the call for him to be loaned out is expected soon.

The feeling is that Mastantuono would benefit for an Endrick Felipe-style loan during the upcoming campaign. The Brazilian forward, who also had a difficult start to his Real Madrid career, saw his stock rise on the back of a successful four-month spell at Lyon during the second half of last season, and now he’s seen as being ahead of the Argentine in the pecking order on the right side of attack.

Mastantuono is prepared to accept a loan exit this summer, knowing that he will not play very much if he stays at Real Madrid. In terms of possible destinations, he is wanted by former head coach Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham, while Serie A side Fiorentina are also showing interest in taking him to Florence for the 2026-27 season.

However, Real Madrid would prefer Mastantuono to go somewhere else. Their desire would be for him to play for a club involved in European competition, as was the case with Endrick at Lyon. Clubs that fall into this category could enter the race in the coming weeks, but until then, the likelihood is that Fulham are favourites due to Arbeloa’s connection with the Bernabeu club.

fullText:
WSL Full-Time were informed of the news via an official club press release from The Golden Girls this morning.

The 30-year-old stopper joins Watford after leaving fellow Barclays WSL2 club Sunderland earlier this summer at the end of her contract. Lambourne spent two seasons on Wearside. She made 28 appearances for The Lady Black Cats in all competitions.

Lambourne started her career at former second tier club Oxford United before enjoying six years with Leicester City. She was a member of the Foxes side that won Barclays WSL2 in 2020/2021. Lambourne often acted as a back-up keeper during her time with the East Midlands club and she had loan spells with Coventry United and Crystal Palace to get more minutes under her belt in her latter days at The King Power Stadium.

The keeper will now hope to use her experience to help Watford compete strongly in Barclays WSL2 this season. The Golden Girls won the FA Women’s National League Southern Premier Division last season and they will now be keen to cement their place in the second tier.

Lambourne is Watford’s fifth signing of the summer transfer window.

title: Sanju Samson unfairly dropped? Abhishek Sharma's failure vs Zimbabwe attracts severe criticism from Indian fans
description: With his third cheap dismissal in as many matches, fans are no longer in the mood to tolerate Abhishek Sharma's batting failures while Sanju Samson was dropped.
fullText:
Sanju Samson unfairly dropped? Abhishek Sharma's failure vs Zimbabwe attracts severe criticism from Indian fans originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Abhishek Sharma's failure against Zimbabwe has drawn heavy criticism from fans.

Many argue Sanju Samson was harshly dropped despite his World Cup heroics.

Samson was named Player of the Tournament at the 2026 T20 World Cup.

India might have sealed their T20I series against Zimbabwe with a 90-run win in Harare on Saturday, but the comfortable result did little to quiet a growing debate about the make-up of their top order. With the third T20I remaining and India eyeing a 3-0 whitewash, all eyes were on their opening duo.

Abhishek Sharma, India's number one-ranked T20I batter, fell cheaply once again, dismissed by Blessing Muzarabani for just 2 runs off 4 balls.

This comes after Sharma was dismissed for 1(8) and 8(8) in the last two matches. It extended a lean run for the opener across the tour and reignited questions about a player who is not even in the squad.

That player is Sanju Samson. The wicketkeeper was named Player of the Tournament at the 2026 T20 World Cup yet finds himself rested for this series, and Abhishek's struggles have led many fans to brand his omission deeply unfair.

MORE: 'Why not Samson?': Srikkanth questions India team management's contrasting treatment

The criticism was led by Sushant Mehta, founder of the Sports Yaari Network, who questioned the logic of persisting with Abhishek while a World Cup star sat out. "6th consecutive failure for Abhishek Sharma; remember T20WC player of the tournament Sanju Samson has been dropped. Unfair?" he wrote.

6th Consecutive failure for Abhishek Sharma, remember T20WC player of the tournament — Sanju Samson has been dropped. Unfair?

— Sushant Mehta (@SushantNMehta) July 26, 2026

Meanwhile, others pointed out that Sharma hasn't been integral to India's success and highlighted inconsistencies in the selection process. One fan aptly wrote, "Abhishek Sharma hasn't even been able to perform against a smaller team like Zimbabwe. Where is the equality? Why does Sanju Samson always have to sit out? Treat the World Cup-winning player with the respect and opportunities he deserves."

Abhishek Sharma hasn't even been able to perform against a smaller team like Zimbabwe. Where is the equality? Why does Sanju Samson always have to sit out? Treat the World Cup-winning player with the respect and opportunities he deserves #Sanjusamson#INDVSZIM@BCCI

— Jas (@JitheeshE22459) July 26, 2026

Other supporters echoed the sense of a double standard. "Sanju Samson got dropped from the team just after 4 failures, and Abhishek Sharma is India's main opener after failing in the whole World Cup," one fan posted. "Also failed in the last 3 T20I series. Different rules for different players."

Sanju Samson got dropped from the team just after 4 failures and Abhishek Sharma is India's main opener after failing in whole World Cup.

Also failed in the last 3 T20I Series. Different rules for Different players. 🙏 pic.twitter.com/sXdOckhYYw

— Soman. (@Shreyasian96) July 26, 2026

But while some were still civil, others didn't put any filter and made even blunter comparisons. "So Abhishek Sharma can fail multiple numbers of times, and still he will get more chances and won't be dropped, but Sanju Samson, who made India win T20WC and performed in 3 crucial games, will get dropped after just 3 failures as always," they wrote.

So Abhishek Sharma can fail multiple numbers of times and still he will get more chances and won't be dropped but Sanju Samson who made India win T20WC and performed in 3 crucial games will get dropped after just 3 failure as always.

— Riken (@97off50) July 26, 2026

One reaction went further, alleging favouritism from the team management, a claim that reflects the fan's own view rather than any established fact. "Abhishek Sharma failed again, but the selectors and coach only dropped Sanju Samson," the fan posted. "They won't drop Abhishek Sharma because he is a puppet of GG."

Abishek sharma failed again but the selectors and coach only drop sanju samson
They won’t drop abishek sharma because he is a puppet of GG
In world cup no good innings and he scored 50 only in finals and 2 time good score he scored after wc but they drop inly sanju#banGG

— Pravanchan Selvam (@Pravanchanselva) July 26, 2026

The direct allegations against Gautam Gambhir echo a feeling that has been felt by Indian fans for a long time now considering the names that have been part of the Indian squads. While India's status as the T20 champions has kept these statements mellow, the current form of Sharma has made the fans much more vocal.

MORE: Hardik Pandya trade: MI want CSK duo as part of swap deal

The frustration is easy to sympathise with. Samson was one of the heroes of India's World Cup triumph, and watching him carry drinks while an out-of-form opener keeps his place naturally feels inconsistent to supporters who value recent achievement.

The picture is more complicated than the posts suggest, however. Abhishek and Samson are not direct replacements for one another, and India's team management has clearly identified Abhishek as its first-choice opener for the next World Cup cycle rather than a short-term option.

That does not entirely excuse the selection. Backing a player through poor form is defensible, but the same patience must eventually be extended to Samson, and India cannot keep justifying one man's place on potential while dropping another on results alone.

title: BREAKING: PSG Superstar Rejects New Contract Proposal
description: According to several different high level and high profile reports on Sunday (the 26th of July 2026), Bradley Barcola has rejected PSG's contract extension.
fullText:
Earlier on today, Sunday the 26th of July, it was reported by Loic Tanzi, amongst others, that PSG winger Bradley Barcola - who is contracted until 2028 - has rejected a contract extension offer from the club.

He states that the reasons are sporting, he is not happy with his game time, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Arsenal listed as sides interested in signing the France international.

Meanwhile, Djameel reports that Barcola was frustrated to find himself on the bench during important games, though he will not force a move away, and has already turned down the aforementioned Chelsea. He also reports that Yan Diomande is the priority replacement. Finally from Djameel, he says that Barcola's priority move is Liverpool.

Elsewhere, Santi Aouna has reported that talks between Liverpool and PSG have already opened discussions regarding a potential transfer. Abdellah Boulma is reporting that PSG want Barcola's replacement signed before sanctioning his sale, and that he will only be sold if the club receives a "major offer".

Fabrizio Romano has also stated that the winger wants to join Liverpool, with the Merseyside outfit "actively working on the deal" and waiting for PSG to "communicate their demands".

Fellow journalist Ben Jacobs has said that Luis Enrique's strategy is clear, as he wants players committed to PSG's project, and that a starting spot is not guaranteed. He also reports that PSG's asking price is 170 million Euros, with Liverpool hoping they can reduce that. The club have pointed to the fees paid for the likes of Elliot Anderson (to Manchester City), and Morgan Rogers (to Chelsea), as a benchmark for what they can demand.

So, there you have all the reports from today. All largely marrying up with each other. What we know is that Barcola wants to leave PSG this summer, and his preferred destination is Liverpool. We also know that the club will not let him go on the cheap, despite the refusal to sign a new contract.

The problem then is, if his asking price is not met this summer, he would then only have one year remaining on his contract next summer, leaving the club somewhat powerless as to fee they can demand, so that is something worth keeping an eye on for sure. Certainly does not feel like the last we will hear regarding Barcola this summer, let's see.

title: Rutgers will be one of USC's few Big Ten 'breather' games in 2026
description: Rutgers will be the perfect tune-up game for USC prior to the matchup versus rival Oregon. If USC does it right, starters won't play too much
fullText:
The Rutgers Scarlet Knights could not afford to lose talent this offseason, especially on the offensive side of the ball. Losing starting quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis is significant; he was the engine for the offense. The Scarlet Knights have two solid pieces on offense in Antwan Raymond and KJ Duff; however, those two can not make up for other holes on this roster.

In a recent article, Bjorn Bergstrom projects the Rutgers Scarlet Knights to take a step in the wrong direction this upcoming season. Here is what he had to say:

"Given the loss of experienced quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, the Scarlet Knights don't project to be very good offensively. Running back Antwan Raymond will have to carry a heavy load in his second season as the starter. Those issues, combined with a porous defense, mean a winless season in conference play could be on the table."

Rutgers finished the season 5-7 last year, and they were one of the better bottom teams in the conference. This season, they will be competing with the Purdue Boilermakers for the worst team according to Bergstrom's projection. Rutgers has special players that can go off for individual great performances, but this team will be a team that top-tier teams like the USC Trojans will need to take advantage of for their own seeding in the standings. USC will face Rutgers in Week 4, and that will be the perfect tune-up game prior to a game with a lot at stake vs the Oregon Ducks.

title: Duke Recruiting: Beckham Black Update - A Brotherhood Assist From Banchero?
description: Paolo Banchero may be a surprise factor in this recruiting battle.
fullText:
A lot of schools are after Beckham Black. Widely regarded as (at least) one of the top two point guards in the class of ‘27, Black is certainly considering schools like Texas, Arkansas, and Duke.

His brother, Anthony, played for the Razorbacks, and is now with the Orlando Magic, where he is teammates with former Blue Devils Wendell Carter and Paolo Banchero. And Banchero is where this story takes a turn.

According to BestofArkansasSports.com, Banchero and the younger Black have become close, and Banchero is pushing Duke. Will it matter in the end?

And for what it’s worth, Anthony Black played for Eric Musselman, who left Arkansas for USC, thus opening the job for John Calipari.

Calipari, of course, has recruited brilliantly for a very long time, and is a formidable rival. However, this is worth noting: he has not gotten a team past the Sweet Sixteen since 2019, and hasn’t made it back to the Final Four since 2015.

Still, he’s a factor, and Duke can’t overlook him, or Texas, or whoever else may pop up. But it’s nice to have a Banchero on your side, too.

title: Red Wings newcomer shines in Triple-A debut despite loss to Buffalo
description: Leandro Pineda went 2-for-3 and scored in his Triple-A debut, but Rochester managed one run in a 3-1 loss to Buffalo.
fullText:
Rochester's pitching kept the game within reach, but the offense couldn't generate enough support in a 3-1 loss to Buffalo at Sahlen Field on Saturday night.

Luis Perales allowed two runs on two hits over five innings, walking five and striking out four. The right-hander's biggest setback came in the fourth inning when Je'Von Ward connected on a two-run homer that gave the Bisons a lead they never surrendered. Buffalo added an insurance run in the seventh.

Leandro Pineda provided a bright spot in his Triple-A debut, going 2-for-3 and scoring Rochester's lone run. Pineda singled in the sixth inning, moved into scoring position after Phillip Glasser drew a walk and later scored on Brady House's sacrifice fly.

The Red Wings finished 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and left five runners on base as Buffalo relievers struck out six batters over the final three innings to close out the win.
