title: Twins overcome another rocky start to advance at State
description: Jul. 26—They call him "The Hammer." That's the Lewis-Clark Twins' nickname for third baseman and pitcher Carson Henson, a rising junior at Lewiston High who has fit right in with the AA Lewis-Clark club, after being called up from the Cubs midway through the summer. He has fit in so well that the Lewis-Clark Twins are bound for the championship round of the American Legion baseball Idaho AA ...
fullText:
Jul. 26—They call him "The Hammer."

That's the Lewis-Clark Twins' nickname for third baseman and pitcher Carson Henson, a rising junior at Lewiston High who has fit right in with the AA Lewis-Clark club, after being called up from the Cubs midway through the summer.

He has fit in so well that the Lewis-Clark Twins are bound for the championship round of the American Legion baseball Idaho AA state tournament largely thanks to his contributions.

"I just love him. We call him 'The Hammer'," said Twins shortstop Guy Krasselt, who in August will report back to Harris Field for his freshman year with the Lewis-Clark State College baseball program. "He's just fun to play with. He's quiet, but he plays hard, and I mean, just gets to work. So it's always fun having him up there because you know he's going to do something good."

Henson stepped onto the mound in a tense situation with the bases loaded in the bottom of the fifth, fired three scoreless innings to close out the win, and slapped a single to spark a three-run seventh inning in the Lewis-Clark Twins' 10-6 win over the Twin Falls Cowboys on Saturday at Harris Field in Lewiston.

The Twins will face the Idaho Falls Bandits at 4 p.m. today back at Harris Field. With a 3-0 record over the past three days, Lewis-Clark is guaranteed to play for the state championship on Monday in the double-elimination tournament.

"I don't think the boys quite knew what was going on, so it was fun to be able to tell them in the huddle out there and say, 'Hey, your hard work's paying off, and your tenacity's paying off. And now we're in the championship,'" Twins coach Micah Brown said. "And we still got a little bit of work left to do, but it feels good to be in the driver's seat."

That's because the right-hander entered with the bases loaded and the Twins' lead sitting at two runs.

Henson permitted one of his inherited runners to score off a sacrifice-fly, then had to deal with another bases loaded situation after an error from Krasselt.

However, two straight flyouts did the trick and Henson escaped the inning unscathed.

"Carson's one of our most reliable guys," Brown said. "He's got command of his pitches, and it's fun to watch him come out and just challenge hitters."

Through three innings pitched, Henson shut out the Cowboys, allowing one hit, with one strikeout and no walks.

After Krasselt's error loaded the bases in the seventh, Henson was in his teammate's ear.

"I was telling him he's gonna make another (play)," Henson said.

In the bottom of the seventh, Krasselt bounded to his right, stayed on his feet and directed the weight of his throw back to his left toward first base for the bang-bang play. The first-base umpire ruled the runner out and the Twins were two outs away from the championship round.

"It's awesome," Henson said of playing with Krasselt. "You always trust him back there at shortstop. He'll get the job done."

Twins pitcher Cody Ells used 34 pitches to trudge through a tough first frame in which the Cowboys harvested five runs off five hits.

Ells struck out two, including the Cowboys' nine-hole hitter, quickly beginning his dismount of the mound and walking back to the dugout as soon as he got that strike three call.

Ells largely settled in from there, firing three consecutive scoreless innings, striking out five, while walking three. However, he ran into trouble in the bottom of the fifth, allowing a walk, a single and hitting the Cowboys' seventh-hole hitter with a pitch before he was lifted for Henson.

Brown said he was proud of Ells' grit.

"It's the beauty of having nine guys in a lineup," Brown said. "If you don't have your stuff that day, there's an opportunity for everybody to pick you up, and that's what these guys are starting to figure out. It's okay to fail."

Picking Ells up is precisely what the Twins did — even if it took a few more innings than the prior day's game.

After a double play left the Twins runless with the bases loaded in the second, the Twins loaded the bases again and came away with two runs.

However, the Twins' own mistakes and miscalculations left some runs off the board, when Green was caught between third base and home for the third out of the inning, leaving Lewis-Clark in a 5-2 hole.

Soon, however, the Twins' patience paid off, and the team began to make its own luck, just like it had the day prior.

The luck came in the form of an infield hit off Krasselt's bat in the fifth that fell directly in front of the plate. Krasselt raced to first as Twin Falls proved unable to make the play.

Later in that inning, the luck appeared as "the foul that never was," — a dribbler off the bat of Jackson Casey that the Twin Falls' pitcher could only stare at as it snailed to a stop and Makhi Durrett scored to cut the Cowboys' lead to one, 5-4.

A Henson sacrifice-fly tied the game, a Grady Peterson double gave the Twins a 6-5 lead and a Ty Collins hard-hit grounder extended that advantage to 7-5 to cap an explosive five-run fifth.

Krasselt said that the players have grown to trust each other over the course of the summer.

It's that trust that continued to motivate the team while down early and the roller coaster of big plays that fired up the dugout throughout the contest.

The dugout was perhaps no more alive than in the top of the seventh, when Peyton Bonebrake slapped a two-run double to left that put the Twins up 9-6.

"It just shines the light on our tenacity as a team, our ability to overcome the rocky start that we had, stay together and chip away," Brown said. "We don't have to do this all at once. Just keep with our plan, chip away at this lead, and we'll have our big inning when it happens."

During the next two days, Lewis-Clark has the chance to accomplish what they have been talking about all summer.

The Twins could win the state championship. Win or lose Sunday, Lewis-Clark will be in the championship round on Monday, with a win that day clinching the state championship.

"I knew we had a good group of guys, and we started off hot," Krasselt said. "And as the season went on, (we) just ended up trusting each other a lot more, trust my coaches, just trust ourselves. So I mean, I thought we had a good chance. Our coach's been saying it since the start."

Brown said he knew this group was capable of playing for such an opportunity when he and his staff put the roster of local All-Stars together in the spring.

For Krasselt, the focus of the next few days is clear.

"Play for each other," Krasselt said. "Just come out with energy and just keep doing what we're doing."

title: Charlton sign Republic of Ireland winger Alli
description: Charlton Athletic sign winger Millenic Alli from Luton Town for an undisclosed fee.
fullText:
Charlton Athletic have signed winger Millenic Alli from Luton Town for an undisclosed fee.

The 26-year-old Republic of Ireland international arrives at the Addicks on a four-year deal after scoring five goals in 38 appearances for the Hatters.

Alli, who Luton signed from Exeter City for a reported £1.5m in January 2025, spent the end of last season on loan at Portsmouth.

"He [Alli] is hungry, he's ambitious, he wants to do really well at this level and kick-on," said Charlton boss Nathan Jones.

Alli becomes Jones' fifth signing of the summer window, following the arrivals of Ivan Mesik, Billy Koumetio, Karlan Grant and Danny McNamara.

title: Casemiro makes Inter Miami debut despite MLS investigation into transfer
description: Casemiro plays, Messi sits out during his post-World Cup rest, and Suarez scores to give Miami a sixth straight MLS win.
fullText:
Brazilian midfielder Casemiro made his debut for Inter Miami despite an ongoing investigation by Major League Soccer (MLS) into his transfer to the United States club.

The former Manchester United man played the full match as Inter Miami defeated Montreal 1-0 on Saturday. Last week, MLS said it was investigating a “tampering allegation” against the club following Casemiro’s arrival.

The league’s inquiry cast a shadow over the midfielder’s arrival, with MLS saying it would withhold details of a settlement between Inter Miami and LA Galaxy over Casemiro’s “discovery rights” until the review concludes.

Under MLS rules, clubs must negotiate discovery rights with any team that previously listed a player before signing him outside the draft or free agency. The Galaxy had held rights to Casemiro before he opted to join Miami instead.

Miami’s 1-0 win in Canada came courtesy of an 81st-minute Luis Suarez penalty. The spot kick was awarded after German Berterame banged heads with Montreal defender Efrain Morales in the box.

Berterame was knocked unconscious and taken away in an ambulance following the collision.

Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos confirmed after the match that Berterame was conscious and “doing well”.

“The blow was very strong, but he is recovering,” Hoyos added.

Suarez sent a soft shot past Sebastian Breza for his ninth goal of the season and his sixth in the last three matches to give Inter Miami their sixth straight victory.

Lionel Messi was rested once again as he continues his recovery following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final.

fullText:
Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are both interested in signing Rodri (30) from Manchester City this summer. According to a report from L’Équipe, PSG’s bid for the Spanish international midfielder could be seen as a counterblow to the La Liga outfit have they accelerated their interest in Les Parisiens’ priority target Yan Diomande (19) from RB Leipzig.

The Ligue 1 champions had previously reached an agreement with the Côte d’Ivoire international on personal terms. However, now that Madrid have entered the race for his services, he has now agreed to join the Spanish capital club and they are now negotiating a deal with the Bundesliga outfit.

Real Madrid have made no secret of their desires to sign the Manchester City midfielder. With the Spanish club now proceeding ahead with signing Diomande, the French capital club have expressed their interest in the Ballon d’Or winner. Even if Rodri only intends to sign for Madrid, PSG’s interest will only ramp up his asking price.

title: ‘Truly a Joke’ — NBA World Rips Warriors Owner Joe Lacob’s Controversial Decision to Focus on ‘Post-Steph Curry Era’
description: The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.

Unsurprisingly, Kawakami’s report sparked a major buzz in the NBA world.

The Warriors’ offseason began with grand visions of landing James after Draymond Green declined a $27.7 million player option to create salary-cap flexibility.

The plan met a major snag as the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar reportedly wanted the Warriors to sign Washington Wizards center Anthony Davis, whom the Wizards were unwilling to trade.

Still, the allure of joining forces with Curry delayed James’ decision before the four-time MVP eventually signed with the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.

From trying to build a legendary lineup, Lacob has seemingly quit on the Warriors’ franchise icon. According to Kawakami, the billionaire will rebuild in the “post-Steph Curry era.”

The viral report drew strong reactions from the WNBA community.

“What a shame. Steph Curry is still one of the best players in the world. To not make an effort to win another title with him is truly a joke. And if you’re not gonna do that, then you have to trade him. Instead, the Warriors are just wasting Steph’s final years. So sad,” NBA analyst Kevin O’Connor tweeted.

“Stephen Curry gets to finish his career where and when he wants. The Warriors can’t trade him unless he asks them to. But in pure basketball terms, it’s better for everyone if he asks for a trade. Golden State’s window is closed, and he’s too good for an extended retirement tour,” CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn added.

“Bro, they doing Steph dirty like that,” an X user wrote.

“They wasted the last 7 years just lucked into 1 championship, so it’s not talked about,” another X user added.

“Joe Lacob has been trying to build post Steph for 8 years now. He brought in a bunch of draft picks (that all sucked) for a post Steph era only for Steph to win the Championship despite this,” another user added.

With James going East, the Warriors’ biggest offseason move left is likely re-signing Green.

After retaining Kristaps Porzingis and De’Anthony Melton and adding Charles Bassey, Golden State’s roster is practically set for the 2026-27 season.

So, the Warriors, which finished this past season with a 37-45 record, will start the new campaign without Butler and Moses Moody. While both rehab from injuries, the Dubs are desperately hoping the oft-injured Porzingis stays healthy, the 40-year-old Al Horford provides quality minutes, and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributes.

Meanwhile, the Oklahoma City Thunder are stronger than ever and are looking to regain their crown. The San Antonio Spurs not only gained valuable playoff experience but also retooled.

Other contenders like the Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves have also made major offseason moves, making the stacked West even more competitive.

Lacob is essentially asking the 38-year-old Curry to keep a hobbled, aging roster afloat, a rinse-and-repeat situation that has often ended in disappointment for the superstar point guard and the team.

Until Curry retires or asks for a trade, this could be the familiar scenario Dubs Nation will be looking at.

title: Patriots claim WR Kobe Prentice off waivers
description: The Patriots added a wide receiver to their roster on Saturday.
fullText:
The Patriots added a wide receiver to their roster on Saturday.

They announced that they have claimed wide receiver Kobe Prentice off of waivers. Prentice was dropped by the Panthers on Friday.

Prentice signed with the Panthers after going undrafted out of Baylor in April. He had 26 receptions for 380 yards and six touchdowns in his final college season.

The Patriots waived offensive lineman Sebastian Gutierrez in a corresponding move. Gutierrez entered the league as an undrafted free agent with the Broncos in 2022 and has had stints with a number of teams, including a couple of tours on the New England practice squad. He has appeared in two regular season games.

title: Roma close on Castro for €35m, Dovbyk targeted by Bologna, Rashford too expensive
description: Roma are reportedly closing on a €35m deal for Bologna striker Santiago Castro, with Artem Dovbyk likely going the other way on loan, as Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United wages rule him out.The ...
fullText:
Roma are reportedly closing on a €35m deal for Bologna striker Santiago Castro, with Artem Dovbyk likely going the other way on loan, as Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United wages rule him out.

The Giallorossi continue their desperate search for reinforcements in attack, having missed out on targets like Mason Greenwood, Crysencio Summerville and Nicolò Tresoldi.

BOLOGNA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 11: Santiago Castro of Bologna celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Coppa Italia match between Bologna FC and SS Lazio at Renato Dall’Ara Stadium on February 11, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

According to Sky Sport Italia, Sportitalia and more, negotiations are at a very advanced stage between Roma and Bologna for Castro.

The asking price is €35m and it can be achieved including bonuses and a percentage of the future sale fee.

ROME, ITALY – MARCH 19: Santiago Castro of Bologna celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Round of 16 Second Leg match between AS Roma and Bologna FC 1909 at Stadio Olimpico on March 19, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

Personal terms should not be an issue for the Argentina international, who turns 22 in September and joined Bologna in January 2024 from Velez Sarsfield for €13.2m.

Able to play in a variety of forward roles, Castro’s versatility has drawn interest from Gian Piero Gasperini.

BOLOGNA, ITALY – DECEMBER 04: Santiago Castro of Bologna celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Coppa Italia Round of 16 match between Bologna FC and Parma Calcio at Renato Dall’Ara Stadium on December 04, 2025 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

It is also widely reported that Dovbyk should go to Bologna on loan, an arrangement they would be more open to with the Rossoblu than with Genoa.

This would not be part of the Castro deal, but rather another matter being discussed between the two clubs.

Meanwhile, Fabrizio Romano’s colleague Matteo Moretto noted that intermediaries had proposed Rashford to Roma after his loan spell at Barcelona.

However, the sheer cost of the salary he currently earns at Manchester United makes that practically impossible.

title: 12 Georgia Bulldogs earn All-SEC selections
description: Twelve Georgia Bulldogs earned preseason All-SEC honors as the team looks to secure another SEC championship
fullText:
The Georgia Bulldogs have 12 players on the preseason All-SEC teams. Georgia has six players on offense and six players on defense across the three All-SEC teams with no Georgia special teams players earning All-SEC honors from the media.

The media predicts that Georgia will win the SEC championship with the Bulldogs being the most popular choice over the Texas Longhorns. A third straight SEC championship would be awesome, but Georgia fans want to see the Bulldogs have more success in the College Football Playoff this season.

Georgia had three players earn All-SEC first-team honors: center Drew Bobo, safety KJ Bolden and cornerback Ellis Robinson. title: Bradley Barcola rejects PSG contract extension amid Bayern Munich interest
description: Bayern Munich and several of Europe’s top clubs may have been handed a significant boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola after reports emerged that the winger has rejected a contract extension a...
fullText:
Bayern Munich and several of Europe’s top clubs may have been handed a significant boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola after reports emerged that the winger has rejected a contract extension at Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG have been attempting to tie the France international down to a new long-term deal for several months, but negotiations have so far failed to produce an agreement.

According to Fabrizio Romano, Barcola has rejected the latest renewal offer from the reigning UEFA Champions League winners and has informed the club that he has no intention of extending his current contract.

Those claims have been reinforced by L’Équipe, which also reports that the 23-year-old is unwilling to sign a new deal in the French capital, fuelling speculation over a potential departure.

Liverpool are currently believed to be leading the race for Barcola’s signature, while Bayern Munich have long admired the versatile forward and continue to monitor his situation closely.

Any move from the Bundesliga champions is likely to depend on developments elsewhere in the transfer market, particularly the future of Luis Díaz, who continues to attract strong interest from Saudi Arabia. Bayern are expected to reassess their options should the Colombian leave.

Despite the growing uncertainty surrounding Barcola’s future, PSG are under no pressure to sell and would reportedly only consider offers in the region of €120 million. Such a fee would make any deal one of the biggest transfers of the summer.

title: ‘Not Fair to This Fan Base’ – NBA Analysts Rip Cavaliers’ Offseason ‘Failure’ After LeBron James Free-Agency Snub
description: LeBron James made it clear that his top priority in choosing his next team was the opportunity to compete for championships and experience winning again, with financial considerations playing no role in his decision. That created a realistic opening for the Cleveland Cavaliers amid their salary-cap limitations, but they were unable to capitalize on it, leaving questions about the team’s disappointing offseason.
fullText:
LeBron James made it clear that his top priority in choosing his next team was the opportunity to compete for championships and experience winning again, with financial considerations playing no role in his decision.

That created a realistic opening for the Cleveland Cavaliers amid their salary-cap limitations, but they were unable to capitalize on it, leaving questions about the team’s disappointing offseason.

Several explanations have emerged for why the Cavaliers were unable to secure James, who began his NBA career in Cleveland before returning for a second stint.

Many expected the Akron, Ohio, native to return, but the 41-year-old made it clear that family considerations did not influence his decision, and he ultimately signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

ESPN analyst Brian Windhorst explicitly mentioned two more reasons for the Cavaliers’ failure in James’ pursuit.

The first was that the Cavaliers’ front office did not trade for Jaylen Brown. Adding a player of Brown’s caliber could have heavily changed James’ perception of the Cavaliers’ championship outlook.

As Windhorst reported, Cleveland also dealt away Darius Garland to acquire James Harden. As Garland was represented by Klutch Sports, keeping him could have helped create a more favorable environment for a reunion.

DON’T MISS: LeBron James Rumors: Eastern Conference Contender Rejected NBA Legend’s Interest Before 76ers Move

As free agency progressed, Cleveland remained largely inactive, seemingly preserving roster flexibility in hopes of landing James.

That cautious approach ultimately backfired, triggering analyst Earl D Mauldin to criticize the team’s offseason strategy.

“That’s distasteful to hear that was why you were in a holding pattern,” Mauldin said on 92.3 The Fan.

“Why the hell were you not more active making moves prior to this? Like, if you really felt in your heart that it was a possibility, but your possibility wasn’t that strong… That’s not fair to this fan base.”

“When Dan Gilbert said that we are nowhere close to where we need to be, and we will be dug in all summer doing whatever we can to improve this roster, that don’t sound like the Cavaliers was dug in all summer doing whatever they can.”

However, Cleveland could still make a big move by acquiring Jonathan Kuminga in a potential deal.

Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson previously coached Kuminga with the Golden State Warriors, making a reunion in Cleveland a realistic possibility that could help energize a frustrated fan base after a quiet offseason.

MORE: ‘There Were 3 Strikes Against Cleveland’ — ESPN’s Brian Windhorst Reveals Why LeBron James Chose 76ers Over Cavaliers

Co-host Spencer German also labeled the Cavaliers’ offseason a disappointment but believes the team still has time to reshape the narrative.

“Right now, this offseason can’t be called anything but a failure…yes, they have more time to see what they can do,” German said. “We might walk away feeling better, maybe not as good as we’d feel if LeBron was here..But we might walk away feeling better about the state of things right now if they get Kuminga or they trade for somebody.”

“But as things stand right now, they’ve failed to improve this roster while other teams in the conference have gotten better.”

So far, Cleveland’s biggest offseason move has been signing Donovan Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million extension.

However, after parting ways with Dean Wade, Keon Ellis, and Larry Nance Jr., the Cavaliers still have work to do to improve a roster that finished 52-30 last season before being swept by the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals.

title: Malaysia Joins F1 2026 Calendar As Host Of Bahrain Grand Prix
description: The Bahrain Grand Prix will be rescheduled to take place in October at the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia.
fullText:
The Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia is set to host the Bahrain Grand Prix from October 2-4, Formula 1 announced Sunday.

Earlier this year, F1 confirmed that April’s races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia would not take place due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Both countries have been targets of Iranian missiles and drones in response to the military attacks by the United States and Israel on Iran that began on February 28.

The prospect of holding both the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix at a later date this year seemed highly unlikely, with only one possibly making a return if any rescheduling were to happen.

FORBES | By Yara Elshebiny
F1 Cancels Bahrain And Saudi Arabian Grands Prix Amid Middle East War

But now after the Malaysian government agreed to host the race this year on behalf of the Gulf country given the instability in the region, the Bahrain GP will make a comeback to the calendar at the beginning of October, taking place at the iconic Sepang International Circuit.

“We are delighted to confirm that Malaysia will host the Bahrain Grand Prix in 2026,” Stefano Domenicali, president and CEO of F1, said. “Once again, the sport has demonstrated its ability to adapt, find solutions, and deliver, creating an exciting moment for everyone who follows Formula 1.”

The return of the Bahrain GP in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, creates a triple-header with Azerbaijan and Singapore, running from September 26 to October 11.

The F1 2026 calendar now features 23 races, with only one event canceled.

“This is fantastic news for our fans,” Domenicali added. “They will continue to enjoy a full and exciting Formula 1 calendar, while also seeing the sport return to a great venue. Malaysia is an incredible country, and Sepang holds a special place in Formula 1 history.

“It will provide a spectacular setting for racing and an unforgettable experience for fans at the circuit and watching around the world.”

Kuala Lumpur first joined as a venue on the F1 calendar in 1999, with the last race held there in 2017 where Max Verstappen celebrated his second career victory with Red Bull.

The past week at Little Ceasar’s Arena has been quite busy, even if the NHL season still isn’t due to start for almost more than two months now. The World Junior Summer Showcase going on next week in Windsor, Ontario has Team USA temporarily using the Red Wings home as their training center, and for three of the members of the 47 man roster, it isn’t an entirely unfamiliar environment.

Red Wings prospects JP Hurlbert, Victor Plante, and Brent Solomon have been in attendance, battling it out and training with the top US junior hockey players in the country over the past week. Drafted over the last two years in Detroit, the trio aim bring a medal to Team USA this summer instead of a Cup for Hockeytown.

The USA’s Team White selected the three to their roster, giving the Red Wings’ prospects what may have been a sneak preview of what their future could look like in the NHL as teammates.

The Red Wings could certainly use a line of high skill, high motor players like them. Set to lose three of their top five goal scorers from the past season, Detroit needs to add more offense to the roster, and fast. Unfortunately, the Hurlbert, Solomon, and Plante are likely out a few years from doing so in a Red Wings sweater, but all three still have plenty of upside as well.

Marco Kasper looks to be recovering well from the knee injury that required offseason surgery. While Kasper suffered from a very hard crash back down to Earth after the highs of his rookie season, there’s still potential for the young Austrian forward to be a top six contributor. title: El Paso Locomotive steams past Sporting Jax in soccer
description: Sporting Jax had a penalty kick saved and went down to a shutout loss on the road in USL Championship men's soccer.
fullText:
Locomotive chugs past Sporting: Amando Moreno scores a point-blank finish 15 minutes in and Rubio Rubin turned a long dribbling run into a tap-in finish late as El Paso Locomotive FC downed Sporting Club Jacksonville 2-0 in USL Championship men's soccer on July 26 at Southwest University Park in El Paso, Texas.

title: Micah Morris could benefit from the Eagles’ proven OL development plan
description: Micah Morris faces an uphill climb, but the Eagles' need to develop depth could create opportunities sooner than many late-round rookies experience.
fullText:
For most NFL teams, the Philadelphia Eagles included, expectations begin changing the deeper the NFL draft progresses. Organizations hope first-round picks develop into Pro Bowlers, All-Pros and, if everything breaks right, future Hall of Famers. Second-round selections are often expected to contribute immediately.

The middle rounds are where championship rosters are built. They're where reliable starters are produced, and valuable role players are discovered. By the sixth and seventh rounds, however, the conversation changes. Teams are no longer searching for immediate contributors. They're looking for players who can stick.

The Philadelphia Eagles have spent years proving those expectations don't always apply. Jason Kelce worked his way into the Hall of Fame discussion after arriving as a sixth-round selection.

Trent Cole developed into one of the franchise's greatest pass rushers after hearing his name called in the fifth round. Jordan Mailata transformed from an Australian rugby player into one of the NFL's premier left tackles after being drafted in the seventh round. At the same time, Jalen Mills carved out a long career as a dependable starter after entering the league as another seventh-round pick.

Micah Morris would love to become the next exception. Every Day 3 pick enters training camp with something to prove. Few enter an organization that has invested more heavily in offensive line development than Philadelphia. Few have prior experience in sparring with what might be the league's best defensive tackle tandem. Morris was a collegiate teammate of Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter.

The Eagles don't simply fill out their roster with young offensive linemen. They actively develop them. That's how Mailata became one of the league's premier tackles. It's how Jason Kelce evolved into one of the greatest centers in franchise history.

More recently, Cam Jurgens successfully navigated the daunting task of replacing Kelce after years of preparation. That developmental philosophy gives every young offensive lineman a reason to believe an opportunity exists. Morris is no different.

At first glance, Morris appears to face an uphill battle. The Eagles return one of the NFL's premier offensive lines. At the same time, veteran Michael Jordan joins younger players such as Myles Hinton, Drew Kendall, Cameron Williams, Hollin Pierce, Jake Majors, Willie Lampkin and Jaeden Roberts in competing for valuable roster and practice squad spots.

Look a little closer, though, and Morris' path becomes easier to envision. Philadelphia has long valued carrying young offensive linemen capable of developing into future contributors. The organization also isn't afraid to keep multiple developmental linemen when it believes they're worthy of long-term investment. Morris doesn't necessarily have to outperform established starters. He has to convince the Eagles he's part of their next wave.

Training camp won't only evaluate Morris. It will also begin evaluating new offensive line coach Chris Kuper. Replacing Jeff Stoutland means more than coaching one of the NFL's best starting offensive lines. It means continuing one of football's most respected developmental programs.

Every rep Morris receives becomes an opportunity for both men. For Morris, it's a chance to prove he belongs in Philadelphia's long-term plans. For Kuper, it's one of the first opportunities to demonstrate that he can continue to transform raw talent into reliable NFL contributors.

History suggests late-round selections face difficult odds. History also suggests the Eagles aren't afraid to challenge conventional thinking. Philadelphia has repeatedly uncovered contributors long after many teams stopped expecting to find them. While comparing any rookie to Jason Kelce or Jordan Mailata would be unfair, their careers serve as reminders that draft position doesn't dictate a player's ceiling.

Micah Morris still has plenty to prove before he earns a regular-season role. Still, unlike many sixth-round selections around the league, he enters training camp with something just as valuable as talent. He enters with a legitimate opportunity.

title: Muhammad Saidov wondered how he'd feed family before UFC call came
description: One of the most impressive performances on UFC Abu Dhabi belonged to debutant Muhammad Saidov.
fullText:
It's been quite the few weeks for recent UFC debutant Muhammad Saidov.

Not only did he get the call-up he'd long sought, Saidov (10-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC) made the most of the opportunity Saturday when he put together a highlight reel second-round TKO barrage to finish Dustin Jacoby at UFC Fight Night 282 at Etihad Arena on Yas Island, Abu Dhai.

"It's very positive emotions," Saidov said post-fight (via UFC). "I was very glad I got to get the victory. I was able to bring happiness to the people that came to support me, to all my people. I was able to show myself on such a big arena. Thank you very much. It's very positive emotions."

Saidov, 30, got the short-notice call up to fight Jacoby (22-10-1 MMA, 10-7-1 UFC) when multiple other opponents withdrew. It was an elevated entry point compared to what many debutants get. But Saidov said he felt right at home.

"I was ready to win. I was ready to lose," Saidov said. "My goal was to just come out and show a good fight. Obviously, Dustin is very, very experienced. He's a great guy but he's a little older. I'm a little faster. Sometimes you have a good day in the office. Sometimes you have a bad one. I didn't have expectations. I happened to have a good one. Everybody says how experienced he is, how good of a kickboxer he is. But I'm also not over here from reading books in the library. I've had a career behind me as well. I can show myself. I can show I belong here. I'm happy that it worked either way. Understand that this is not anything special. This is my work. I came out here. I did my job well and that's what it was."

With the victory, Saidov takes home his show money, win money, and $25,000 finish bonus. The cash couldn't come at a better time. Just prior to receiving the UFC call, Saidov admits he debated stepping away from competition entirely as his bank account was running low.

"Honestly, I really hope that I won some fans over and somebody is going to know who I am now," Saidov said. "A month ago, I was sitting at home and I didn't know where to get the money to feed my family. I was going to quit this sport. I was going to find something different. To be honest, I don't think about fans or whatever. I am not in a place where I can feed my family and I'm excited I'm here in the UFC to do it."

title: Yankees All-Star abruptly pulled from game on Saturday
description: Another crucial loss for the Yankees lineup.
fullText:
The New York Yankees picked up an important victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Saturday, but the win may have come at a significant cost. All-Star outfielder Cody Bellinger was forced to leave the game early after suffering what appeared to be a hamstring injury, creating another major injury concern for a Yankees team that has already been hit hard by key absences. With the MLB trade deadline looming, Bellinger’s status could have a significant impact on New York’s plans.

While the Yankees were already expected to be aggressive in pursuing upgrades, another injury to the middle of their lineup may force the front office to become even more active.

MORE: One player every MLB team will trade at the 2026 trade deadline

Bellinger exited Saturday’s game after appearing to injure his hamstring, and the Yankees will now anxiously await the results of further medical testing.

The veteran outfielder is expected to undergo additional evaluations, with more information on the severity of the injury likely becoming available within the next 24 to 48 hours.

Until those results are known, the Yankees can only hope the injury is a minor one. Losing Bellinger for any extended period would be a significant blow to a lineup that has already been forced to overcome several key injuries.

MORE: 5 MLB pitchers who will be traded before the trade deadline

The timing couldn’t be much worse for the Yankees.

Aaron Judge remains sidelined, while Giancarlo Stanton still does not have a timetable for his return. Those absences have already placed added pressure on the rest of New York’s offense, making Bellinger one of the club’s most important bats in the middle of the order.

If Bellinger is forced to miss significant time, the Yankees would suddenly find themselves without three of their biggest offensive threats during one of the most critical stretches of the season.

MORE: Longest MLB winning streaks this century

Even before Saturday’s injury, New York was widely expected to be among the most aggressive buyers ahead of the MLB trade deadline. Now, the severity of Bellinger’s injury could alter those plans even further.

If testing reveals a lengthy absence, the Yankees may shift their focus toward acquiring another impact outfielder in addition to addressing other roster needs. The front office has the prospect depth to pursue several different avenues, and another significant injury would only increase the urgency to make a move.

For now, the Yankees and their fans will wait for the medical update. The club earned an important win over the Phillies on Saturday, but the biggest news may ultimately be Bellinger’s health. The results of his upcoming tests could shape not only New York’s lineup for the remainder of the season, but also its approach to the trade deadline.

title: Could study into head injuries change women's rugby?
description: Head contact affects women differently yet rugby's concussion guidelines are still largely based on the men's game, something Cardiff University is looking to change.
fullText:
Former players have backed ground-breaking new research into the impact of concussion in women's rugby.

Repeated blows to the head have been found to affect women differently to men, with female athletes more susceptible to concussion and reporting longer recovery times.

Symptoms can also vary, with men more likely to experience amnesia, while a proportionately greater number of women report prolonged headaches, mental fatigue and difficulty concentrating.

But despite the findings, rugby's concussion guidelines are still largely based solely on the men's game - something ex-internationals say needs to change.

Cardiff University's medical engineering team is now aiming to create the first head impact assessment protocol designed specifically for female athletes.

The study followed 30 players from the university's women's rugby team, using specialised mouthguards, cognitive tests and MRI imaging.

Researchers hope to gather enough data by the end of the year to determine whether new guidelines can be set.

"The female brain is different from the male brain and women's rugby is different from male rugby, so if we were only to use the same safety threshold as we do for men, that would seem inconsistent with the evidence that we understand so far," said lead researcher Peter Theobald.

Elinor Snowsill, capped 76 times during a 14-year international career, is among those backing the female-focused research.

"We are not just mini versions of men," she said.

"It is so important to understand our bodies and that we have systems in place that are best suited for us, not just taken from the men's game.

"There is no game [of rugby] that is more important than your brain.

"It is the one thing you cannot replace. You can rehab any muscle or have a knee replacement, but you have to have your brain for the rest of your life. Nothing is more important than your health."

Uncertainty surrounds why women can experience concussion differently to men, although researchers point to brain structure and neck strength.

This is alongside differences in the way the game is played, in strength and conditioning and the later introduction of women to the sport.

But the lack of dedicated research into the women's game is not unique to rugby with only 6% of sports science research solely based on female athletes, according to PhD student Freya Butcher, part of the research team.

"We aim to contribute to that pool and gain a better understanding of the way that female physiology interacts with our sports," she said.

While welcoming their work, former Wales wing Caryl James says it is concerning that only now research is being done into female athletes.

"That really worries me and I feel women have definitely been let down over the years," she said.

I've been playing rugby since I was eight, I never thought about concussion - until now

What are rugby union's rules on concussion injuries?

The mouthguards being used by the university team are similar to those used by World Rugby in elite competitions.

They measure the force, speed and direction of head impacts, with medical staff alerted if they exceed a set threshold. Players are then required to leave the pitch for a head injury assessment (HIA).

However, part of the research aims to uncover whether those thresholds should be refined specifically to the women's game.

Cleo Pallister-Turley plays rugby for Cardiff University's rugby team and says the study has made the whole team more aware of concussion.

"Both on and off the pitch, the study has made the whole team a little bit more wary about head health, in a way that throughout my 13 years of playing rugby hasn't been spoken about," she said.

"The previous season I would have just got up after any hit to the head and thought it was fine to play on.

"But last season, you're a lot more aware of it, even though the data wasn't fed back to us."

Awareness was something that former Wales centre Alecs Donovan says was lacking during her playing career.

"It wasn't the coaches or the medical team that knew I was concussed because I carried on playing, it was at work a couple of days after," Donovan said.

"I worked as a medical rep. I was in operating theatre and one of the doctors there said he thought I was concussed, just because of how I was feeling."

Snowsill added: "I remember playing and thinking that one of the women had hit her head, but at the time other players didn't know how important it was.

"They just knew it would mean they wouldn't be able to play, so a lot of the players would try to hide it, and I would question whether I should report it.

"Although it's your friend, you want to do what's best for them even if they would be angry with you for doing so."

High Court leaves rugby brain injury case in balance

Smart gumshields - chips, change and criticism

Smart mouthguards a 'game-changer' for rugby union

The impact of concussion has come to the forefront of rugby with hundreds of former players bringing legal action against the sport's governing bodies.

English World Cup-winners Steve Thompson, Mark Regan and Phil Vickery as well as Welsh British and Irish Lions Ryan Jones, Gavin Henson and Dafydd James claim authorities failed to protect them from the neurological consequences of repeated head impacts and concussions.

That six-year battle hangs in the balance following two days of High Court proceedings this week as the judge considers whether the claimants have complied with an order to provide documents surrounding the neurological testing process.

But despite the well-documented risks, Pallister-Turley hopes Cardiff's research will not deter people from playing rugby.

"The idea of this research is not to scaremonger, it's to invest in more research that allows you to make an educated and informed decision about your head health," she said.

"The sport is great in terms of friendships and camaraderie; it means so much to so many people."

title: Paddle UK chief hails GB start to LA28 qualification
description: The British team start their Olympic qualification campaign with third place in the medal table at the ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships in Oklahoma City.
fullText:
Paddle UK performance director Tom Duggan said he is proud of the British team after they started their Olympic qualification campaign with third place in the medal table at the ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships in Oklahoma City.

Sam Leaver won the team's sixth medal, and his first at senior level, at the World Championships, with kayak cross bronze at the venue set to be used for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

GB's other medals came from Joe Clarke's gold in the men's kayak cross, the men's team winning the canoe team world title, Adam Burgess' silver in the men's canoe final, Lois Leaver – Sam Leaver's sister - winning bronze in the women's kayak cross individual and Kimberley Woods winning women's kayak bronze.

"I am really pleased with the performances we put in this week. It has been a really good start to the Olympic Qualification System," said Duggan, after GB finished behind the Czech Republic and Australia.

"It is only the first race of nine for the rankings but to have achieved some of the performances we have on what will be the Olympic venue is really important as we build confidence and momentum.

"The conditions have been really difficult in terms of the temperatures for the athletes and coaches to contend with, but it has given us a flavour of what to expect in 2028.

"I am super proud of how everyone, athletes and coaches, have come together to put in the performances we have."

title: 68 fights unbeaten - now teenager White is aiming for gold
description: Teenage boxer Ruby White hopes her unbeaten run of 68 fights will take her to Commonwealth Games gold on her debut.
fullText:
Despite a run of 68 fights undefeated across her fledgling career, teenage boxer Ruby White was far from expecting a Commonwealth Games call-up when the phone rang.

The 19-year-old had "no clue" when Rob McCracken, performance director of GB Boxing who has trained Anthony Joshua and Carl Froch, wanted to speak to her earlier this summer.

"I was dog sitting at the time," White told BBC Radio Somerset.

"One of my coaches, Ben Stewart, he text me and said, 'Let me know when you've got off the phone to Rob [McCracken]' and I thought 'Oh gosh, why is Rob calling me, am I in trouble?'"

White only joined the Great Britain Boxing academy in May but has been rising through the amateur and junior ranks since she started boxing aged seven.

Her 5ft 1in stature has earned her the nickname the 'Pocket Rocket' and among her accolades are seven national championships, four European titles for England and the under-19 world title in 2024 among her unbroken list of victories.

In February she clinched the Golden Girls Boxing Cup in Sweden, a competition where more than 500 female boxers from all over the world took part.

When selection to compete in Glasgow came, White said she did not think she had ever been so happy in her life.

"[Rob] called me and I was like, 'You're lying, there's no way' and he was like 'You're young and you're hungry and we know you can do well'. I was ecstatic," she said.

The carpenter aiming for Commonwealth boxing glory

Center Parcs to CWG bronze, now gold for Yeats Brown?

White, from Sturminster Newton in Dorset, will compete in the flyweight 51kg class and is among 14 boxers selected for England who are all making their competition debut.

For many of Britain's biggest boxing stars, the Commonwealth Games has proved a major stepping stone in their career, with Nicola Adams and Lauren Price among those to have clinched gold in recent editions - two people White takes inspiration from.

"This is the very beginning of my worldwide career journey as an elite," she said.

"I want to follow in the same footsteps as Nicola Adams and Lauren Price, all those big names who have been training in the GB setup like I am.

"I want to come back with gold from the Commonwealth's and then the next step is the the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles."

White's first fight is on Monday (18:30 BST) against South Africa's Thandolwethu Mathiba and she admits she will likely be "very nervous" when she steps into the SEC Arena for the first time.

"I'm just going to take it one day at a time and I know I'm meant to be there," she said.

"All the training's been done, the hard work's been done in the gym I just need to perform and put on a good display of boxing."

That being said, the teenager is relishing the prospect that her form coming into the Commonwealth Games had made her a target for others.

"I haven't lost since I was 11 and every time I step in that ring I know that my opponent wants to take my unbeaten record from me," White said.

"It's a lot of pressure but in know that means I care."

She added: "I get in that ring each time and think me and my opponent both want that victory, both want to win and both want to do well but I want it more."

title: Scotland upset Wales for first win of Commonwealths
description: Scotland defeat Wales in an all-British clash at The Hydro in Glasgow at the Commonwealth Games
fullText:
Scotland bounced back from defeat to New Zealand with a 56-47 win over Wales at The Hydro in Glasgow.

The hosts started brightly as they raced into a 16-8 first quarter lead.

A better second quarter for the visitors saw Wales reduce the deficit to just two goals before Scotland rallied to a 28-21 half-time lead.

Emma Barrie's dominant shooting saw Scotland take a ten-goal advantage into the final quarter.

Niamh McCall, a teammate of nine of the Welsh team at Superleague side Dragons caused constant problems with her shooting from distance.

Wales gave away too many contact penalties throughout the game to cut into the lead.

Scotland held firm to secure their first win of the Games.

They face 12th ranked Trinidad and Tobago in their next match on Monday night.

Wales will play the same opponents on Tuesday as they seek their first win in Glasgow.

Scotland goal attack Niamh McCall said:

"Ecstatic, this was one we were targeting.

"We beat them in November, they're ranked higher than us so to be able to double down on that we are so happy that we won today.

"Kath [Tetley] always talks about step by step so we take each day at a time and we'll look back at today and what we can do better and very much focus on Trinidad tomorrow.

"We definitely need to use the crowd to our advantage, they are like the eighth player on the court for us, so the louder they can be the better and it was phenomenal today.

Wales captain Bethan Dyke said:

"Bitterly disappointed, that first quarter is where we let it go really.

"I think to come back in those other three quarters there wasn't much in it, just not good enough in the first quarter.

"We can't shy away from the fact that this isn't where we wanted to be but there's still a lot to play for in this competition.

"We've got a rest day tomorrow and we have to come back stronger in our next game."

title: Normandy's D-Day World War Two beaches become UNESCO heritage site
description: PARIS, July 26 (Reuters) - The Normandy D-Day beaches where Allied forces landed on June 6, 1944, to fight Adolf Hitler's Nazi troops and go on to liberate France have become a UNESCO protected world
fullText:
PARIS, July 26 (Reuters) - The Normandy D-Day beaches where Allied forces landed on June ‌6, 1944, to fight Adolf Hitler's ‌Nazi troops and go on to liberate France have become ​a UNESCO protected world heritage site, the United Nations body said on Sunday.

• In a statement on its website, UNESCO said that the ‌beaches formed an "exceptional ⁠cultural landscape shaped both by the events of 1944 and by their ⁠enduring remembrance", which therefore justified becoming a protected heritage site.

• The Normandy D-Day beaches are ​regularly the ​focus of commemorations ​featuring world leaders from ‌the United States, Britain, Canada and France.

• Soldiers participating in the Normandy landings came from the United States, Britain, Canada, Belgium, Norway, Poland, Luxembourg, Greece, Czechoslovakia, New Zealand and Australia. ‌Some 177 French commandos also ​took part.

• The assault ​marked a decisive ​stage in the liberation of Europe ‌from Nazi Germany in ​World War ​Two.

• In total, 156,115 Allied troops either landed by sea -- on to beaches codenamed ​Utah, Omaha, Gold, ‌Juno and Sword -- or were airdropped behind ​German coastal defences.

description: Firms like Northrop Grumman are struggling on the market despite record military spending. Investors are now watching Congress—and a new generation of startups.
fullText:
The U.S. has racked up a $37.5 billion tab on the war in Iran following President Donald Trump's launch of Operation Epic Fury in late February. Yet despite continued conflict and historic levels of defense spending requested by the Pentagon, investors betting on a defense windfall have watched many top contractors lose value.

How do defense contractors' record backlogs impact future performance?

What role are defense tech startups playing in Pentagon contracts?

Why are defense stocks declining despite increased war spending?

When do defense investments typically generate the best returns?

Trading volumes in major defense contractors surged in the conflict's opening days—rising for some as much as 140% above their average level during Trump's second term—but the gains didn't last. Northrop Grumman is now down over 30%, L3Harris Technologies has fallen over 20%, and Lockheed Martin has declined nearly 13%. Raytheon Technologies (RTX)—No. 49 on the Fortune 500—was at one point down about 18%, though the stock has since recovered to up 4% after the company reported better-than-expected second-quarter earnings.

At first glance, the selloff seems counterintuitive. The Pentagon has fired thousands of high-end munitions during the conflict, including more than 1,000 Tomahawk cruise missiles and hundreds of THAAD, Patriot, and SM-3 interceptors to protect U.S. and allied forces, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Replenishing those depleted stockpiles is likely to benefit defense contractors, on top of the Trump administration's push for a $1.5 trillion defense budget—a 42% increase.

Markets, however, have remained unimpressed. According to Guy Rozentsveig, managing director in industries at investment bank Solomon Partners, one reason is simple: "The consensus opinion is that a lot of that good news was already priced in."

Now, investors hunting for the industry's next payday are waiting to see whether higher defense budgets actually translate into new contracts, faster production, and stronger earnings—or whether political and economic pressures slow long-term momentum. Meanwhile, a growing group of newer defense technology companies is hoping to capture a piece of that future spending, too.

Determining whether defense stocks are worthwhile investments takes more than comparing quarterly earnings or even how many missiles are fired alone—it's often largely centered on how much governments commit to spending in the years ahead.

That's why, according to Mike Derrios, executive director of the Baroni Center for Government Contracting at George Mason University, the best returns in defense often come long before a conflict begins.

"Investor 'alpha' is most likely gained when investments are made before wars and before legislated funding, not after a war has begun, become unpopular, or when associated plus-ups are in doubt," Derrios told Fortune.

title: California authorities search for 2 children allegedly abducted by father, fear for their safety
description: Solomon and Marozhina Sukonick were last seen in Lancaster with their father, and authorities say there is concern for the abducted children's well-being.
fullText:
Authorities in California are searching for two 9-year-old children who investigators say were abducted by their father this week, warning there is concern for their well-being.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department is asking for the public's help locating Solomon and Marozhina Sukonick, who investigators say were taken by their father, David Sukonick, on Thursday.

According to authorities, the children were last seen around 8 p.m. near the 1000 block of West Avenue J-8 in Lancaster.

Man Accused Of Killing Partner Arrested In Mexico Nearly Two Years After Fleeing With Their Two Children

The sheriff's department said in a news release there is "concern for their well-being," urging anyone with information to come forward.

Investigators said the children were last seen traveling in a black 2011 Lincoln Town Car with California license plate SOLOYST.

Marozhina is described as a 9-year-old White girl who stands 4 feet, 4 inches tall and weighs about 90 pounds. She has brown hair and brown eyes and was last seen wearing pink shorts and a white shirt.

Malnourished Boy Found Locked In Father's Van For More Than A Year Unable To Walk, Hadn't Showered Since 2024

Solomon, also 9, is described as a White boy who stands 4 feet, 4 inches tall and weighs about 90 pounds. He has brown hair and brown eyes and was last seen wearing blue shorts and an unknown-colored shirt.

David Sukonick is described as a 71-year-old White man who stands 5 feet, 7 inches tall, weighs about 135 pounds and has brown hair and green eyes.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department at 661-940-3855.

Anonymous tips can also be submitted through L.A. Regional Crime Stoppers by calling 800-222-TIPS (8477), using the P3 Tips mobile app or visiting lacrimestoppers.org.

According to the New York Post, David Sukonick shared a photo of the children on Facebook on July 13. One commenter questioned whether the children were OK, writing that they looked "miserable."

title: France and Spain battle wildfires as more than 250,000 people are forced to flee homes
description: LEGE-CAP FERRET, France (AP) — France sent a hulking military cargo plane to dump tons of flame retardants as it battled raging wildfires on Saturday and slashed the final stage of Tour de France to r...
fullText:
LEGE-CAP FERRET, France (AP) — France sent a hulking military cargo plane to dump tons of flame retardants as it battled raging wildfires on Saturday and slashed the final stage of Tour de France to redeploy security personnel to the blazes that forced tens of thousands of people to flee their homes.

The latest wildfires in southern Europe this week have displaced more than 250,000 people, including some 70,000 people who were evacuated in central Spain. One man died in Manises, the municipality reported on its Facebook page, the first death so far in the blazes.

In France, the giant A400M transporter swooped in low, its long plume of ochre-colored retardant trailing over drought-hit woodlands in the southwest as fire crews on the ground fought flames that authorities feared could spread toward the wine region city of Bordeaux.

Race organizers and the Paris police department announced a truncated 21st and final stage on Sunday for the three-week Tour, France's most famous annual sporting event, reflecting the immense strain that two large fires in the southwest are causing for emergency services.

Tour riders will race Sunday inside Paris, rather than starting from Thoiry, west of the capital, on a circuit of 89 kilometers (55 miles) — down by a third from the 133-kilometer (82.5-mile) route that had been planned. Part of the race's security detail will instead "reinforce the response efforts in the areas affected by the wildfires," according to the statement announcing the "exceptional measures made necessary by the situation."

With winds expected to shift in a west-to-east direction on Saturday afternoon, potentially driving flames closer to Bordeaux, fire crews and authorities were digging trenches, using retardants and taking other blaze-blocking steps, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, predicting a "long and very difficult" battle.

He said the fire was about 30 kilometers (20 miles) west of the city and lost some of its intensity overnight. The prefect of the Gironde region that includes Bordeaux said the blaze grew into "a firestorm" on Friday after igniting earlier this week and cautioned that it "remains dangerous" even though firefighters were making progress.

The government mobilized soldiers to join fire crews and was rushing in 1.5 million face masks to protect against choking smoke.

Authorities ordered people between the fire and Bordeaux to evacuate, including from parts of the city's western suburbs and other towns and villages.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described the fires as unprecedented and said the Gironde blaze became so strong on Friday that it had begun generating its own winds. Firefighting teams were being reinforced with the addition of hundreds of soldiers and breathing masks to filter out potentially noxious smoke particles were being rushed to those exposed, Lecornu said.

In Bordeaux, authorities took in thousands of evacuees, offering them food and shelter in an exhibition center, and the city's mayor said it could be equipped to welcome as many as 10,000 people if that became necessary. The city's airport said it remained open but that its bus and tram services were suspended.

Evacuation orders were sent with special alerts to mobile phones, instructing people to leave, Gironde prefect Sophie Brocas said. She said the fire had destroyed about 140 homes in the region.

The French military A400M transport plane, specially converted for fire-fighting, was a heavyweight new tool in the battle. It joined at least 18 other water- and retardant-dropping aircraft and helicopters that Nunez said were deployed in the Gironde region, working in rotation in the smoke-filled skies.

The virulence of the French and Spanish wildfires, fueled by high temperatures and the long-term effects of climate change, caught fire crews and authorities off guard.

Firefighters in Spain said the blazes spread so fast and violently that they could not be tackled head on. In France, some people even fled by boat when flames swept through touristic towns on the Atlantic coast.

"We've never seen anything like this," said Javier Organista, a resident of El Tiemblo, west of Madrid, where fire charred a famed chestnut grove. "When we saw the flames coming into our town, surrounding us, leaving us with practically no way out, all the neighbors joined together to try to stop its advance."

"It's just really sad," he said.

Spain deployed 2,600 firefighters, police and other emergency personnel to two blazes west of Madrid, backed by 19 water-dumping aircraft and helicopters.

France deployed 1,400 firefighters to the Gironde fire and hundreds of others to another wildfire further south in the Landes region. Dozens of firefighters suffered injuries, authorities said amid panic scenes with townsfolk fleeing by car and police went door to door to tell people to leave.

Successive heat waves that hit unusually early and hard this year, baking Europe with record-shattering high temperatures, have turned forests and scrublands into tinderboxes.

Fires have burned 130,000 hectares of forest already this year in Spain, up from an annual average of 100,000 hectares over the past decade, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Saturday as he visited a command post west of Madrid.

He said more favorable weather Saturday offered "a window of opportunity" for fire crews to bring the blazes under control. Madrid's regional government said the fires decreased in intensity as winds and temperatures dropped.

The fatality reported on Saturday occurred in Manises, part of the wildfire-affected region of Valencia.

Other European nations were helping, with Italy, Greece, the Netherlands, Portugal, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Sweden, Slovakia, Germany and Switzerland already providing or expected to deploy water-dumping planes and helicopters to the Spanish and French fire fronts.

Leicester reported from Paris. Associated Press journalists Barry Hatton in Lisbon, Portugal; Manu Fernandez in El Tiemblo, Spain; and Joseph Wilson in Barcelona contributed.

title: Corporate America may be using AI to cut jobs, but small businesses are using it to keep them
description:
Reports of wide-scale replacement of workers by AI are overblown. Small businesses use it to help workers
I recently met the owner of a company that sells windows and doors. He told me he invested about $10,000 in an AI application that is used by his salespeople in his showroom.
